classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless multiplier that limits particle flux transport for one
specified ionization charge state relative to its free-streaming bound.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state particle flux limiter coefficient sets the maximum
permitted particle-flux density for one specified ionization charge state
relative to its free-streaming bound.

$$
\left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s} \right\rVert \leq f_s \left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{fs},s} \right\rVert
$$

where $f_s$ is the flux limiter coefficient, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}$ is
the particle flux density of the specified ion charge state,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{fs},s}$ is its free-streaming particle-flux
bound, and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes vector magnitude.

The coefficient applies to particle transport for the selected ion charge
state, including thermal and nonthermal contributions when represented. It
is not summed over ion charge states and does not limit energy or momentum
transport. The corresponding [ion charge-state particle
flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) is the bounded vector quantity;
this coefficient is not itself a flux. The particle-channel limitation is
distinct from the [ion momentum flux limiter
coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which applies to
momentum transport.

items.name: parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed field-aligned effective velocity whose product with neutral energy
density gives the convective neutral-energy flux in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral-energy convection velocity is the effective coefficient of
the energy-density-proportional advective flux of neutral energy in the edge
plasma. It describes directed energy transport after gradient-driven
transport has been separated.

The parallel convective energy flux is defined by

$$
F_{n,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = U_n v_{n,\parallel}^{E}
$$

where $F_{n,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-parallel neutral-energy
flux due to convection, $U_n$ is the energy density of the selected neutral
population, and $v_{n,\parallel}^{E}$ is this effective convection velocity.

The quantity is the local magnetic-field-aligned projection,
$v_{n,\parallel}^{E}=\mathbf{v}_n^{E}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where
$\mathbf{v}_n^{E}$ is the neutral-energy convection velocity vector and
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local nonzero magnetic
field. It applies to the selected neutral population, not to a sum of
particle-, heat-, and momentum-channel velocities.

It excludes conductive or diffusive energy flux and need not equal the
neutral bulk-flow velocity. The [radial neutral-energy convection
velocity](name:radial_neutral_energy_convection_velocity) describes the
corresponding major-radius projection rather than the field-parallel
projection. This neutral-energy coefficient is distinct from [ion heat
convection velocity](name:ion_heat_convection_velocity), which acts on ion
thermal energy.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral-energy convection is directed along
the local magnetic field.

items.name: inner_radius_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Inner radius of a toroidal field coil is the bore-side radius of an annular
conductor or winding-pack cross-section, measured from the geometric center
of that cross-section to its inner boundary.
items.documentation:
Inner radius of a toroidal field coil is the non-negative radial distance in
the local cross-sectional plane normal to the local conductor or
winding-pack centerline, from the geometric center of an annular
toroidal-field-coil cross-section to its bore-side inner boundary. It
defines the bore size of the annular cross-section, not the spatial location
of the coil.

For an annular cross-section with circular inner and outer boundaries, the
conducting or winding-pack cross-sectional area satisfies:

$$
A = \pi\left(r_\mathrm{outer}^2 - r_\mathrm{inner}^2\right)
$$

where $A$ is the annular cross-sectional area in square meters,
$r_\mathrm{inner}$ is this inner radius in meters, and $r_\mathrm{outer}$ is
the corresponding outer radius in meters.

The quantity is defined for hollow annular conductor or winding-pack
cross-sections and obeys $0 \le r_\mathrm{inner} < r_\mathrm{outer}$; the
limiting value $r_\mathrm{inner}=0$ represents a solid circular
cross-section treated as an annulus with no bore. It is the inner-boundary
member of the toroidal-field-coil cross-section radius family:
outer_radius_of_toroidal_field_coil gives the outer boundary, while
radius_of_toroidal_field_coil denotes a generic non-negative cross-section
radius not tied specifically to the bore-side boundary.

items.name: power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative power associated with a specified plasma heating or
energy-transfer channel, integrated over the volume enclosed by a magnetic
flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined
plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux
surface. The parent does not by itself select a species, population, source,
absorption mechanism, or whether the channel is absorbed power or net
transferred power.

For a volumetric channel power density, the cumulative power is

$$
P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p_{\mathrm{ch}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ch}}(\psi)$ is the cumulative channel power, $\psi$ is the
magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by that
surface, $p_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is the corresponding volumetric power density,
$\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the volume element.

Species- and population-specific instances include [electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), [ion power
at an inside flux surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface), and [ion
charge-state power at an inside flux
surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface). Absorbed-power
channels count energy deposited in the recipient population, whereas
net-transfer channels follow the specified transfer direction and may be
signed.

items.name: thermal_plasma_energy
items.description:
Volume-integrated stored thermal energy of the confined plasma, equal to 3/2
times the volume integral of the total thermal pressure; the thermal
component of total stored plasma energy excluding fast-particle and
electromagnetic-field contributions.
items.documentation:
Thermal plasma energy $W_{th}$ is the internal kinetic energy of the thermal
electron and ion populations within the confined plasma. It excludes
fast-particle energy and electromagnetic-field energy.

For scalar isotropic thermal pressure, it is defined by

$$
W_{th} = \frac{3}{2} \int_V p_{th}\,dV
$$

where $p_{th}$ is the sum of the thermal electron and ion pressures and $V$
is the confined plasma volume. It is the thermal contribution to [plasma
energy](name:plasma_energy).

items.name: etendue_of_line_of_sight
items.description:
Geometric optical throughput of a charge-exchange spectroscopy line of
sight, determined by its collecting aperture and accepted solid angle.
items.documentation:
Étendue is the geometric throughput of the optical collection system
associated with a charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight. It specifies
the channel’s angular and collecting-area acceptance for source radiation.

The étendue $G$ is defined by

$$
G = A\Omega
$$

where $A$ is the collecting aperture area, corresponding to the [diagnostic
aperture area](name:area_of_diagnostic_aperture), and $\Omega$ is the solid
angle of the accepted rays at that aperture.

This quantity describes geometric acceptance only. It excludes detector
efficiency, optical transmission losses, and spectral response; those
factors must be treated separately when relating collected signal to
absolute photon flux.

items.name: diameter_of_pellet
items.description:
Transverse extent of the intact cylindrical pellet before injection and
shattering, defined as the full width of its circular cross-section
perpendicular to the pellet axis.
items.documentation:
Transverse extent of the intact cylindrical pellet before injection and
shattering is the full width of its circular cross-section measured
perpendicular to the pellet axis. It defines the pellet cross-sectional
geometry before fragmentation, ablation, or interaction with the plasma.

For an ideal right circular cylindrical pellet, the diameter and axial
length determine the pellet volume by

$$
V_\mathrm{pellet} = \frac{\pi}{4} d_\mathrm{pellet}^2 L_\mathrm{pellet}
$$

where $V_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the pellet volume, $d_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the
pellet diameter, and $L_\mathrm{pellet}$ is the [length of
pellet](name:length_of_pellet).

This quantity excludes the axial extent of the pellet, which is the [length
of pellet](name:length_of_pellet), and excludes characteristic sizes of
shattered fragments, ablated material, or the post-shattering material
cloud.

items.name: wavelength_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
Vacuum wavelength selected by Bragg diffraction from the crystal lattice
spacing and orientation, defining the central spectral passband of the
crystal.
items.documentation:
The Bragg wavelength is the vacuum electromagnetic wavelength selected by a
crystal's lattice geometry for a specified diffraction order. It defines the
central spectral coordinate of the crystal passband and is distinct from the
pixel-specific assignment represented by [wavelength of detector
pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel).

For lattice planes with spacing $d$ and Bragg angle $\theta_B$, the selected
wavelength satisfies

$$
n\lambda_B = 2d\sin\theta_B
$$

where $\lambda_B$ is the wavelength, $n$ is the positive integer diffraction
order, $d$ is the crystal lattice-plane spacing, and $\theta_B$ is the angle
between the incident beam and the lattice planes. The angle is the crystal
diffraction geometry characterized by [angular width of Bragg
crystal](name:angular_width_of_bragg_crystal).

items.name: thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive
thermal-energy flux of the ion population to its local ion-temperature
gradient, without selecting a transport direction.
items.documentation:
The ion energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,E}$ quantifies gradient-driven
diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by the ion population. It is
the direction-agnostic ion-population coefficient underlying
component-specific quantities such as the [total thermal ion energy
diffusion coefficient](name:total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
and the radial form [radial total thermal ion energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
and is distinct from convective or drift contributions to the ion heat flux.

The defining Fickian relation for the diffusive ion thermal-energy flux is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}} = -n_i D_{i,E}\nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive ion thermal-energy
flux, $n_i$ is the total ion number density, $D_{i,E}$ is the ion energy
diffusion coefficient, $T_i$ is the total-ion temperature expressed as
thermal energy per ion, and $\nabla T_i$ is its spatial gradient.

For a total-ion quantity, the coefficient is the density-weighted mean over
all ion species and charge states. Direction-specific projections, including
the radial component, retain this physical definition while selecting a
transport direction. The leading minus sign specifies down-gradient Fickian
diffusion for a positive coefficient.

items.name: fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total
fast-ion population by background ions, summed over all fast-ion species and
charge states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the
complete fast-ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with
background ions. It aggregates all fast-ion species and charge states
without resolving the receiving fast-ion subpopulation.

The volume-integrated fast-ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}} = \int_V Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $Q_{\mathrm{fast\text{-}ion,coll}}$ is the local collisional
power-exchange density into the aggregate fast-ion population, $\mathbf{r}$
is position, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $V$ is the plasma
volume.

This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion power due to
collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions). Its charge-state-resolved
counterpart is [fast ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), while
[thermal ion power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions) describes transfer
into thermal ions. Internal exchanges among fast-ion species cancel in the
summed net value.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net
energy into the complete fast-ion population.

items.name: binormal_coordinate_of_correction_coil
items.description:
Signed displacement of a correction-coil conductor outline vertex along the
local Frenet–Serret binormal, measured from the conductor centerline.
items.documentation:
The binormal coordinate specifies the signed position of a correction-coil
conductor cross-section outline vertex along the local Frenet–Serret
binormal direction. Together with the [normal coordinate of the correction
coil](name:normal_coordinate_of_correction_coil), it defines the vertex
position in the cross-sectional plane.

For vertex position $\mathbf{r}_v$ and corresponding centerline position
$\mathbf{r}_c$, the coordinate is

$$
b_v = (\mathbf{r}_v - \mathbf{r}_c) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $b_v$ is the binormal coordinate in m, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the local
unit binormal, and $\mathbf{r}_v$ and $\mathbf{r}_c$ are positions in m. The
local Frenet–Serret triad is oriented so that $\hat{\mathbf{b}} =
\hat{\mathbf{t}} \times \hat{\mathbf{n}}$, with $\hat{\mathbf{t}}$ the
tangent and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ the normal unit vector. This coordinate is a
signed vertex displacement, not the full conductor cross-section height
represented by the [height of the correction
coil](name:height_of_correction_coil).

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the conductor
centerline points in the direction of the local unit binormal
$\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: flux_due_to_eddy_current
items.description:
Eddy-current-attributed energy flux is the areal rate at which energy
generated by Joule dissipation of induced eddy currents is transferred
across a surface. It denotes the eddy-current contribution only, not a
generic process-labeled wall flux or total heat flux.
items.documentation:
Eddy-current-attributed energy flux is the areal rate at which energy
generated by Joule dissipation of induced eddy currents is transferred
across a surface. It is a process-attributed scalar energy flux: the process
is fixed to eddy currents, while more specific names may add a locus such as
a wall surface.

The scalar flux is defined as the surface density of eddy-current-attributed
power:

$$
F_{\mathrm{eddy}} = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{eddy}}}{dA}
$$

where $F_{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the eddy-current-attributed energy flux,
$P_{\mathrm{eddy}}$ is the power associated with Joule dissipation of
induced eddy currents, and $A$ is the area over which that power is
distributed.

The scope is the eddy-current contribution in conducting plasma-facing
structures; if several induced-current paths contribute to the same surface
element, their eddy-current-attributed power contributions are summed before
division by area. This quantity excludes total wall heat flux and
energy-flux contributions attributed to radiation, particle impact,
externally applied heating, or non-eddy-current mechanisms, and it does not
by itself specify that the evaluation locus is the wall.

Energy flux due to eddy current is the explicitly energy-qualified form of
this same process-attributed flux. [Flux at wall due to eddy
current](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_eddy_current) is a locus-specialized form
evaluated at a plasma-facing wall; the present quantity retains only the
shared eddy-current mechanism attribution, not that child locus.

items.name: poloidal_electron_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Poloidal component of the electron particle diffusion coefficient. It is the
poloidal-poloidal diagonal tensor component in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ),
where ρ labels magnetic flux surfaces, θ is poloidal angle, and φ is
toroidal angle, relating diffusive electron particle flux to the electron
density gradient along θ.
items.documentation:
The poloidal electron diffusion coefficient is the electron particle
diffusivity acting along the poloidal direction tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ on a magnetic flux surface in flux coordinates
$(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces, $\theta$
is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is toroidal angle. It is the poloidal-poloidal
diagonal component of an anisotropic particle-transport tensor, relating
diffusive electron particle flux to the electron density gradient along that
poloidal tangent.

For a Fickian closure of the diffusive part of the [poloidal electron
particle flux](name:poloidal_electron_particle_flux), the component along
the poloidal tangent satisfies:

$$
\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_{\theta} = -D^{e}_{\theta\theta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\cdot\nabla n_e
$$

where $\Gamma^{e,\mathrm{diff}}_{\theta}$ is the diffusive poloidal
component of the electron particle flux density, $D^{e}_{\theta\theta}$ is
the poloidal electron diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is
the unit tangent in the direction of increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and
$\phi$, and $n_e$ is the electron number density. The minus sign expresses
the down-gradient convention for positive diffusivity.

This is a particle transport quantity, distinct from electron energy
transport such as poloidal_electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient. It
excludes convective contributions to the electron particle flux and
off-diagonal tensor couplings; radial transport across flux surfaces is
represented by radial_electron_diffusion_coefficient, and a
non-direction-specific electron particle diffusivity is represented by
[electron_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of tritium ions averaged over the plasma boundary, summed
over all tritium ion charge states and excluding neutral tritium.
items.documentation:
Number density of tritium

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{T}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{T}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{T}}\rangle$ is the averaged tritium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the local tritium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is summed over all tritium ion charge states and excludes
neutral tritium. It is a flux-surface average, not a local point value,
volume average, or chord average.

The average is formed from the local [tritium density at the plasma
boundary](name:tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary) by applying
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting over the surface. It differs from
the [volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density),
which uses a volume rather than a flux-surface domain.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: current_density_per_toroidal_mode_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
items.description:
Current density per toroidal mode due to wave-driven current drive is the
vector non-inductive current-density contribution from one toroidal Fourier
harmonic. It represents local charge transport produced by wave-particle
interactions before summing over toroidal modes or projecting onto
directions such as the magnetic-field-parallel direction.
items.documentation:
Current density per toroidal mode due to wave-driven current drive is the
vector non-inductive current-density contribution associated with one
toroidal Fourier harmonic of the wave-driven current-drive source. It
represents the local conventional-current response produced by wave-particle
interactions for that harmonic, retaining the vector direction rather than
only a scalar projection.

The toroidal mode number labels Fourier harmonics in toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. The mode-summed wave-driven current
density is related to the per-mode contributions by

$$
\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_n \mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n(\mathbf{x},t)
$$

where $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}$ is the [mode-summed wave-driven current
density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive),
$\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n$ is this per-toroidal-mode vector current
density for toroidal mode number $n$, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and
$t$ is time.

This quantity applies to the wave-driven non-inductive current-density
contribution at a local plasma position and is resolved for a single
toroidal mode. Its aggregation convention is mode-resolved:
per-toroidal-mode means attributed to one harmonic index, not divided by the
number of harmonics, and no sum over $n$ is included. It excludes inductive
or ohmic current density, total plasma current, particle flux, and wave
power.

The [parallel per-toroidal-mode wave-driven current
density](name:parallel_current_density_per_toroidal_mode_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
is the magnetic-field-aligned projection of $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n$
for the same toroidal mode. Summing $\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{WCD}}_n$ over mode
numbers gives the [mode-summed wave-driven current
density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive); it does not
give another per-toroidal-mode quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component represents conventional
current flowing in the positive direction of the component's explicitly
named basis vector or projection direction.

items.name: runaway_electron_diffusivity
items.description:
Directional transport coefficient describing the diffusive spatial spreading
of runaway-electron density through the plasma.
items.documentation:
Runaway-electron diffusivity is the effective coefficient governing spatial
spreading of the runaway-electron population by diffusive transport. Its
directional instances include [perpendicular runaway electron
diffusivity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_diffusivity), which
describes cross-field spreading.

For a resolved transport direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux is
related to the runaway-electron density gradient by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{re,diff},i} = -D_{\mathrm{re},i}\,\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{re}}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{re,diff},i}$ is the diffusive runaway-electron
particle flux, $D_{\mathrm{re},i}$ is the diffusivity for direction $i$,
$n_{\mathrm{re}}$ is the runaway-electron number density, and $x_i$ is the
corresponding spatial coordinate. The quantity describes the diffusive
contribution only and is distinct from the effective convection velocity
represented by [perpendicular runaway electron convection
velocity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_convection_velocity).

items.name: toroidal_electron_velocity
items.description:
Signed component of the local mean electron flow tangent to circles about
the symmetry axis, describing toroidal electron transport in the edge
plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal electron velocity is the signed projection of the local
electron-fluid bulk flow onto the toroidal direction in the edge plasma.
This direction is tangent to circles about the symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{e,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_e \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{e,\phi}$ is the toroidal electron velocity, $\mathbf{v}_e$ is the
local [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the
unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

The underlying electron-fluid velocity is the particle-number-weighted first
moment of the local electron velocity distribution, rather than the
center-of-mass velocity of all plasma species. The toroidal component is a
local linear velocity, not an angular velocity, the full flow magnitude, or
a measure of random thermal motion; no spatial averaging is implied.

The [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) projects the
same electron-fluid velocity along increasing major radius, rather than
around the symmetry axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal electron flow is directed toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: prefill_gas_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of the neutral gas introduced before plasma breakdown, governing
the pressure-dependent ionization conditions for early electron-avalanche
breakdown.
items.documentation:
Prefill gas pressure is the thermodynamic pressure of the neutral gas
present before plasma breakdown. It establishes the gas conditions used in
the Townsend electron-avalanche criterion during plasma initiation.

For an ideal neutral gas, pressure is related to particle density and
temperature by:

$$
p_g = n_g k_B T_g
$$

where $p_g$ is the prefill gas pressure, $n_g$ is the neutral particle
number density, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, and $T_g$ is the neutral-gas
temperature. This ideal-gas relation applies when the ideal-gas
approximation is valid.

This quantity describes the prebreakdown gas state; it is not the
accumulated injected inventory represented by
[prefill_count](name:prefill_count) or the pressure of the plasma formed
after breakdown.

items.name: electron_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective transport velocity that multiplies electron thermal-energy density
to give the convective electron energy flux, appearing as the convective
velocity in the energy flux term; distinct from gradient-driven diffusion
and mean electron flow.
items.documentation:
Electron energy convection velocity is the effective vector coefficient
relating the convective electron thermal-energy flux to the local electron
thermal-energy density. It is the electron-specific specialization of
[energy convection velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity) and appears as
the convective velocity in the energy-flux term.

The convective electron thermal-energy flux density is the product of the
local electron thermal-energy density and this velocity:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_e\,\mathbf{v}_{e,W}
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{e,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective electron
thermal-energy flux density, $\mathcal{W}_e$ is the local electron
thermal-energy density, and $\mathbf{v}_{e,W}$ is the electron energy
convection velocity. The subscripts identify the electron population and the
energy-convection channel.

This quantity applies to electron thermal-energy transport in core and edge
plasma, without restricting it to a spatial direction or aggregating it with
ion or neutral energy transport. It specifies only the convective
contribution to [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux), excluding
gradient-driven diffusion; it is not the total electron energy flux or the
bulk electron particle-flow velocity.

The [radial](name:radial_electron_energy_convection_velocity),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_electron_energy_convection_velocity), and
[parallel](name:parallel_electron_energy_convection_velocity) electron
energy convection velocities are directional projections of this vector. The
radial projection is the $\hat R$ component in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height; the parallel projection is along the local magnetic
field. This energy-transport coefficient need not equal the [electron
particle velocity due to
convection](name:electron_particle_velocity_due_to_convection), which
describes particle rather than energy transport.

Sign convention: Positive when a projected velocity points along its
positive direction; the radial component is positive toward increasing major
radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and the
parallel component is positive along the local magnetic field.

items.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity
items.description:
Vertical current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the signed
symmetry-axis projection of electric current generated by the divergence of
perpendicular viscous stress.
items.documentation:
Vertical current density due to perpendicular viscosity is the local
symmetry-axis projection of the electric-current contribution generated by
the divergence of perpendicular viscous stress in a magnetized charged
plasma.

The component is defined by

$$
j_Z = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $j_Z$ is the signed vertical component, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{pv}}$ is
the [current-density vector due to perpendicular
viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), and the
subscript $\mathrm{pv}$ labels that mechanism. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ points along increasing vertical height in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This is a local, mechanism-resolved contribution to [current
density](name:current_density), not the total vertical current density or a
spatial average. “Perpendicular” identifies the viscous-stress mechanism,
not a restriction of the resulting current vector to directions
perpendicular to the magnetic field. The [parallel component due to
perpendicular
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity)
projects the same vector along the local magnetic-field direction rather
than the symmetry axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the conventional electric-current
contribution due to perpendicular viscosity has a component toward
increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the dimensionless transport of
resolved linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface by the
electric-field drift. Concrete specializations supply the momentum
component, crossing direction, velocity-space contribution, and
normalization reference.
items.documentation:
Normalized momentum flux due to E×B drift is the normalized flux of resolved
linear plasma momentum carried across an oriented surface by the E×B
advective drift. It represents the E×B-drift contribution to turbulent
momentum transport, distinct from the sum over all transport mechanisms.

As a normalized flux, it is the corresponding E×B momentum-flux contribution
divided by the reference momentum flux used for the same normalization
convention:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}^{E\times B}_{a,n} = \frac{\Pi^{E\times B}_{a,n}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\Pi}^{E\times B}_{a,n}$ is the normalized momentum flux due
to E×B drift, $\Pi^{E\times B}_{a,n}$ is the E×B-drift contribution to the
flux of the resolved linear-momentum component $a$ through the oriented
surface normal $n$, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference momentum flux
for the same normalization convention.

This parent quantity does not choose a particular momentum component,
crossing direction, velocity-space contribution, species, or surface
orientation; those are supplied by concrete specializations. For example,
[perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift](name:perpendicular_momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
resolves the perpendicular velocity-space contribution while retaining this
E×B-driven parent mechanism.

It excludes normalized momentum flux produced by mechanisms other than E×B
drift, including electromagnetic contributions associated with
[momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_perturbed_parallel_vector_potential).
It is not the total normalized momentum flux unless the relevant mechanism,
component, and velocity-space contributions have been combined according to
their own definitions.

Sign convention: Positive when positive resolved linear momentum is carried
by the E×B drift in the positive crossing direction specified by the
concrete specialization.

items.name: change_in_ion_state_mean_ionisation_potential
items.description:
Change in ion-state mean ionization potential is the signed difference
between the concentration-weighted mean cumulative ionization potential of
an ion charge-state bundle after and before a specified state change.
items.documentation:
Change in ion-state mean ionization potential is the signed difference in
the ion-state mean ionization potential of an ion charge-state bundle across
a specified state change. The base quantity is the concentration-weighted
mean of the cumulative successive ionization energies required to reach,
from the neutral ground state, the charge states represented in the bundle.

The change is defined as the value after the change minus the value before
the change:

$$
\Delta \bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s} = \bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{after}} - \bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{before}}
$$

where $\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{after}}$ and
$\bar{E}_{\mathrm{ion},s}^{\mathrm{before}}$ are the ion-state mean
ionization potentials of the same ion-state bundle after and before the
change.

This quantity accounts only for the change in the mean cumulative ionization
energy associated with the represented charge-state composition. It excludes
thermal internal energy, excitation energy, radiation losses, and kinetic
energy exchanged during ionization or recombination.

items.name: neutral_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Neutral momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of
linear momentum carried by neutral particles and attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
items.documentation:
Neutral momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of
linear momentum carried by neutral particles and attributed to the
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic contribution. It is the neutral-species
specialization of [momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

With $i$ denoting the transported momentum component and $j$ denoting the
flux direction, the underlying diamagnetic contribution is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,ij} = \rho_n u_{n,i} v^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,j}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,ij}$ is the neutral momentum-flux contribution,
$\rho_n$ is neutral mass density, $u_{n,i}$ is the neutral velocity
component carrying momentum, and $v^{\mathrm{dia}}_{n,j}$ is the velocity
contribution associated with diamagnetic drift.

This quantity includes only the diamagnetic contribution and excludes
neutral momentum flux attributed to other transport mechanisms. It is not
resolved by internal neutral state, unlike [neutral state momentum flux due
to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and the
name imposes no particular momentum component or flux direction.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral momentum is transported in the
positive direction of the oriented flux surface.

items.name: fast_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque on the fast-particle population is the volume-integrated
angular-momentum transfer caused by Coulomb momentum exchange with the
thermal background plasma.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque on the fast-particle population is the angular-momentum
transfer caused by Coulomb collisions with the thermal background plasma,
integrated over the plasma volume. It is the fast-population specialization
of [torque_due_to_collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions), with
axis-resolved forms such as
[toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions);
the corresponding electron-population quantity is
[electron_torque_due_to_collisions](name:electron_torque_due_to_collisions).

The torque about a chosen origin is defined from the collisional force
density by:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the chosen origin,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force
density acting on the fast-particle population, and $V$ is the plasma
volume. The aggregate includes collisional contributions from thermal
electrons and thermal ion species and charge states; electromagnetic forces,
external sources, and noncollisional mechanisms are excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when a torque component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_density
items.description:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into bulk thermal
electrons, including its average over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron power density is the rate at which coherent electromagnetic
waves transfer energy directly to the bulk thermal electron population per
unit physical volume. Its flux-surface-averaged form describes the mean
deposition on a magnetic flux surface; the underlying local quantity
describes deposition within that surface.

The flux-surface-averaged deposition is defined by

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{e,th}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{e,th}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs,e,th}}}{dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\overline{p}_{\mathrm{e,th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged
thermal-electron power density, $p_{\mathrm{e,th}}$ is the local
thermal-electron power density, $P_{\mathrm{abs,e,th}}$ is the coherent-wave
power absorbed by thermal electrons within physical volume $V$, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes an average over the magnetic
flux surface.

The recipient population is restricted to bulk thermal electrons. Absorption
by nonthermal electrons belongs to [fast-electron absorbed wave power
density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density). This quantity is
the direct wave-absorption contribution to [electron power
density](name:electron_power_density), not the net sum of all electron
heating and cooling channels; it excludes [collisional electron energy
exchange](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), including
subsequent collisional redistribution of deposited energy.

[Mode-resolved thermal-electron power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density) specializes
this deposition by individual toroidal Fourier harmonic. Flux-surface
averaging retains the volumetric normalization rather than integrating over
the enclosed volume. Integrating that average with the enclosed-volume
measure gives the [cumulative thermal-electron absorbed power inside the
flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a measurement position, equal to its
perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of measurement position

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal coordinates of the same position in the
right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, whose origin lies on the toroidal
symmetry axis and whose vertical coordinate $z$ is aligned with $Z$.

This quantity evaluates the parent coordinate at the specified measurement
position; no summation, averaging, or weighting is implied. It is
nonnegative and vanishes on the toroidal symmetry axis. It is distinct from
a minor-radius distance measured from the magnetic axis and from a magnetic
flux label.

The [radial coordinate of a line of
sight](name:radial_coordinate_of_line_of_sight) specifically locates that
line's second reference point; this quantity does not impose that
reference-point convention.

items.name: outer_radius_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Outer radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the outer cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section.
items.documentation:
Outer radius of an antenna strap is the perpendicular distance from the
strap conductor axis to the outer cylindrical boundary of its annular
cross-section. It identifies the outer boundary of the conductor material
and is the larger of the two annular boundary radii.

Use [radius of antenna strap](name:radius_of_antenna_strap) for the
boundary-radius concept without selecting a surface, and [inner radius of
antenna strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) for the smaller boundary
radius. If $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ denote the [inner radius of
antenna strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) and the outer radius of
antenna strap, respectively, then $0 \le r_\mathrm{in} \le r_\mathrm{out}$.
This quantity is distinct from the [height of antenna
strap](name:height_of_antenna_strap), [toroidal width of antenna
strap](name:toroidal_width_of_antenna_strap), and [thickness of antenna
strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap).

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
items.description:
Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Poloidal component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the
poloidal component of the vector defined by [ion charge state convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), rather than an energy-
or momentum-transport velocity.

The associated advective particle flux density is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}} = n_z v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{pol}}^{\mathrm{adv}}$ is the poloidal advective
particle flux density, $n_z$ is the number density of charge state $z$, and
$v_{\mathrm{conv},z}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is this velocity component. The
component is expressed in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The charge state is resolved rather than summed over ionization states.
Unqualified convection velocity denotes particle transport; [poloidal ion
charge state energy convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity)
represents the distinct energy-transport channel.

Sign convention: Positive when the component points toward increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: helium_4_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Local particle number density of helium-4 ions evaluated in the boundary
plasma immediately adjacent to the plasma-facing limiter surface, on the
plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance. The value is
summed over He+ and He2+ ionization states and excludes neutral helium-4
atoms.
items.documentation:
Helium-4 density at a limiter is the local number density of helium-4 ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance, not inside the limiter material or in neutral
gas retained at the surface. It is summed over the helium-4 ion charge
states He$^+$ and He$^{2+}$, and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms.

The charge-state-summed helium-4 ion density is related to the
charge-state-resolved velocity distribution functions by:

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} \int f_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v
$$

where $q$ is the positive ion charge state, $f_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}$ is the
velocity distribution function of helium-4 ions with charge state $q+$, and
the integral is taken over all particle velocities at the limiter-side
evaluation point.

This quantity is the helium-4 isotope contribution to
[density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and to the unweighted ion
population represented by
[total_ion_density_at_limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter). In a
quasineutral boundary plasma,
[electron_density_at_limiter](name:electron_density_at_limiter) is coupled
to the charge-weighted ion sum, so helium-4 contributes $\sum_{q=1}^{2}
q\,n_{\mathrm{He4}^{q+}}$ to that balance. The corresponding helium-3
isotope quantity is
[helium_3_density_at_limiter](name:helium_3_density_at_limiter).

items.name: poloidal_neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed effective poloidal velocity coefficient for density-proportional
convective particle transport of a specified neutral state in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient of density-proportional
convective particle transport for a specified neutral state, projected onto
the poloidal direction. It represents directed drift or pinch transport
after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has been separated.

The poloidal convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}} = n_s v_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}$ is the poloidal convective particle
flux, $n_s$ is the particle density of the specified neutral state, and
$v_{n,s}^{\mathrm{conv,pol}}$ is this effective velocity coefficient. The
quantity is the poloidal component of [neutral state particle convection
velocity](name:neutral_state_particle_convection_velocity), not the complete
particle flux and not the diffusive transport coefficient. Its species-state
and particle-channel meaning distinguishes it from the analogous [poloidal
ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity).

items.name: plasma_mass_density
items.description:
Local plasma mass per unit volume, forming the inertial term in the MHD
momentum equation and appearing in contexts from equilibrium transport
profiles to linear MHD stability perturbations.
items.documentation:
The plasma mass density is the local plasma mass per unit volume, forming
the inertial term in the MHD momentum balance and the compressibility term
in the plasma continuity equation. This parent concept subsumes both
equilibrium-profile and linear-perturbation contexts: the equilibrium total
value summed over all charged species, and the complex first-order
perturbation amplitude used in linear MHD eigenvalue problems.

In the equilibrium formulation, the mass density is defined by:

$$
\rho = \sum_s m_s n_s
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass and $n_s$ the number density of charged
species $s$, summed over electrons, main-ion isotopes, and impurity charge
states; neutral atoms are excluded. Ion contributions dominate because $m_i
\gg m_e$.

In deuterium-dominated fusion plasmas at core electron densities of order
$10^{20}$ m$^{-3}$, the mass density is approximately $3 \times 10^{-7}$ kg
m$^{-3}$, scaling directly with ion density and average ion mass. The mass
density sets the local Alfvén speed $v_A = B / \sqrt{\mu_0 \rho}$, where $B$
is the local magnetic-field magnitude and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of
free space, governing the [alfven_time](name:alfven_time) and ideal-MHD wave
dynamics. It enters inertial_current_density through the plasma-fluid
acceleration term and is inferred from electron_number_density measurements
combined with plasma composition analysis. This quantity is closely related
to [mass_density](name:total_plasma_mass_density), which covers the same
physical concept without explicit species qualification.

items.name: coulomb_logarithm
items.description:
Natural logarithm of the effective upper-to-lower impact-parameter ratio
governing cumulative small-angle Coulomb scattering between charged
particles in a plasma.
items.documentation:
The Coulomb logarithm expresses the effective logarithmic range of impact
parameters contributing to cumulative small-angle Coulomb scattering in a
plasma.

The Coulomb logarithm $\ln\Lambda$ is defined by

$$
\ln\Lambda = \ln\left(\frac{b_{\max}}{b_{\min}}\right)
$$

where $\Lambda$ is the effective impact-parameter ratio, $b_{\max}$ is the
upper impact-parameter cutoff, $b_{\min}$ is the lower impact-parameter
cutoff, and $\ln$ denotes the natural logarithm. In a weakly coupled plasma,
screening limits the upper cutoff, while strong deflection or quantum
diffraction sets the lower cutoff; the small-angle approximation requires
well-separated cutoffs.

The unqualified quantity specifies neither a colliding species pair nor a
spatial evaluation point, and implies no species sum or spatial average. The
[Coulomb logarithm at the pedestal
top](name:coulomb_logarithm_at_pedestal_top) is this same quantity evaluated
at the pressure pedestal top.

The logarithm, rather than the impact-parameter ratio itself, enters Coulomb
collision frequencies and collisional resistivity as a multiplicative
factor.

items.name: toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
items.description:
Toroidal current density due to anomalous transport quantifies the signed
conventional-charge flow around the symmetry axis arising from turbulent,
nonclassical plasma transport.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density due to anomalous transport is the signed toroidal
projection of the conventional electric-current contribution attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

The defining projection is

$$
j_\phi = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $j_\phi$ is this toroidal current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the [current density due to anomalous
transport](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The
right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R, \phi, Z)$, where $R$ is the distance
from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

This quantity denotes the local net conventional-charge flux attributed to
anomalous transport, not the total toroidal current density or a
particle-number flux. No spatial or flux-surface averaging is implied.

The [parallel current density due to anomalous
transport](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport)
projects the same vector onto the local magnetic-field direction instead;
the toroidal and parallel components need not coincide.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional electric current flows toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above
along the positive vertical axis.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description:
Full physical extent of the rectangular soft X-ray detector aperture
measured between its two boundaries along the detector-local first
tangential (X1) direction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the full end-to-end width of a soft X-ray detector's
rectangular aperture along its object-local first tangential axis, denoted
X1. It defines one dimension of the detector acceptance geometry used in
etendue calculations.

The width is defined by

$$
w_1 = x_{1,\mathrm{max}} - x_{1,\mathrm{min}}
$$

where $w_1$ is the first-local-tangential aperture width, and
$x_{1,\mathrm{max}}$ and $x_{1,\mathrm{min}}$ are the coordinates of the two
opposing aperture boundaries along X1.

The quantity applies to one soft X-ray detector aperture with rectangular
geometry and represents the complete boundary-to-boundary extent, not a
half-width, an outline coordinate, the second local tangential width, or an
aggregate over multiple detectors. The boundary coordinates used in the
defining difference are provided by the [first local tangential coordinate
of the soft X-ray
detector](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector). The
same geometric convention is used for the corresponding [first local
tangential width of a hard X-ray
detector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector), while
[extent of the soft X-ray detector](name:extent_of_soft_xray_detector)
denotes a broader detector-size quantity rather than this specifically
defined X1 aperture dimension.

items.name: toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description:
Signed toroidal component of the refractive-index vector for a lower-hybrid
wave launched by a lower-hybrid antenna.
items.documentation:
The toroidal launched-wave index is the signed projection of the
refractive-index vector of a wave launched by a lower-hybrid antenna onto
the toroidal direction. It characterizes toroidal phase variation and is
distinct from the dimensional [toroidal wave
vector](name:toroidal_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam).

The index is defined by

$$
n_\phi = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{k_0} = \frac{k_\phi}{k_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched-wave vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit
vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $k_\phi$ is the toroidal projection of
$\mathbf{k}$, and $k_0$ is the free-space wavenumber. The corresponding
poloidal quantity is the [poloidal launched-wave
index](name:poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna).

Sign convention: Positive when the launched-wave vector has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Velocity due to E cross B drift for a specified ion charge state is the
guiding-center drift vector produced by crossed local electric and magnetic
fields, independent of ion mass and charge.
items.documentation:
Velocity due to E cross B drift for a specified ion charge state is the
guiding-center drift vector produced by local crossed electric and magnetic
fields in a magnetized plasma. It is common to all magnetized charged
species at the same position, although this name resolves it to one ion
charge state.

The defining relation is:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{E\times B} = \frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector and $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector. The resulting vector is perpendicular to
$\mathbf{B}$, and its magnitude is the parent [velocity due to E cross B
drift](name:velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

This vector quantity must be distinguished from its signed axis projections,
including the [radial ion charge-state velocity due to E cross B
drift](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) and
[toroidal ion charge-state velocity due to E cross B
drift](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift). The
ion charge-state resolution identifies the represented population but does
not introduce mass- or charge-dependent variation in the drift itself.

items.name: power_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one
divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over
the target's wetted strike-zone surface.
items.documentation:
Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one
divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over
the target's wetted strike-zone surface. The specified channel denotes a
particular physical contribution to deposition and does not by itself imply
an all-channel target total.

The deposited power for target $t$ and channel $c$ is defined from the
channel-resolved energy-flux-density vector over that surface:

$$
P_{t,c} = -\int_{A_t} \mathbf{S}_{E,c}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_t(\mathbf{x}) \, dA
$$

where $P_{t,c}$ is the deposited power on target $t$ due to channel $c$,
$A_t$ is the target's wetted strike-zone surface, $\mathbf{S}_{E,c}$ is the
energy-flux-density vector for channel $c$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_t$ is the
normalized surface normal directed from the target material toward the
plasma-facing side, $\mathbf{x}$ labels a point on the target surface, and
$dA$ is the surface element. The leading minus sign makes flux directed from
the plasma toward the target material contribute to the deposited target
power.

The channel label may distinguish conductive, convective, particle,
radiative, or other deposition mechanisms, but this name does not prescribe
a decomposition. For a complete mutually exclusive set of channel
contributions on the same target, the channel sum equals the surface
integral of the total [energy flux at a divertor
target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target); all-channel target powers at
the inner and outer divertor targets are represented by power at inner
divertor target and power at outer divertor target. Conductive and
convective channel contributions are represented by [power at divertor
target due to conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction)
and [power at divertor target due to
convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), respectively.

items.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux
items.description:
Parallel neutral momentum flux is the signed rate per area at which
magnetic-field-parallel momentum carried by neutral atoms and molecules
crosses an oriented surface, summed over species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral momentum flux is the rate per unit area at which the
magnetic-field-parallel component of neutral [linear
momentum](name:momentum) crosses an oriented surface in the edge plasma. The
parallel qualifier identifies the transported momentum component, not the
direction normal to the transport surface.

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\parallel}(\hat{n}) = \hat{b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0(\hat{n})
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral momentum flux,
$\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit normal to the oriented surface, $\hat{b}$ is
the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0(\hat{n})$ is the vector [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux) across that surface. The subscript $0$
denotes the neutral population.

This quantity includes convective momentum transport and neutral
thermal-pressure contributions, summed over all neutral atomic and molecular
species and their internal states. It excludes charged-particle momentum and
is not restricted to transport along the magnetic field. The [parallel
neutral internal-state momentum
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) resolves an
individual internal-state contribution; summing those contributions over
states and species gives this aggregate.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transferred across the
surface in its chosen normal direction has a component along the local
magnetic field.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species
evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local effective fuel-ion count per
physical volume at that location.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the deuterium-tritium fuel-ion pseudo-species
evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local effective fuel-ion count per
physical volume at that location. It represents the deuterium–tritium
mixture as one effective ion population rather than as separate deuterium
and tritium species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{DT}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT,axis}}$ is the deuterium-tritium pseudo-species number
density at the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the number of effective
deuterium-tritium pseudo-ions, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. The aggregation convention treats the deuterium-tritium mixture as
one effective ion population; this quantity is not separately resolved by
isotope and is neither a flux-surface, line, nor volume average or integral.

This is the deuterium-tritium specialization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [deuterium-tritium density](name:deuterium_tritium_density) by
explicitly fixing the evaluation locus at the magnetic axis rather than
leaving the locus unspecified.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective coefficient relating the poloidal diffusive flux of a neutral
species to its local number-density gradient in the same direction.
items.documentation:
Effective poloidal particle diffusivity for neutral species is the
directional transport coefficient that represents neutral-particle spreading
driven by a neutral number-density gradient. It is the poloidal
specialization of [neutral particle
diffusivity](name:neutral_particle_diffusivity), with transport resolved
around the magnetic axis within a plane of constant toroidal angle.

For the poloidal direction, the diffusive neutral-particle flux is defined
by

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{0,\mathrm{p}}\frac{\partial n_0}{\partial s_{\mathrm{p}}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive
neutral-particle flux density, $D_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal neutral
particle diffusivity, $n_0$ is the neutral-species number density, and
$s_{\mathrm{p}}$ is physical arclength along the poloidal direction. The
minus sign specifies transport down the neutral number-density gradient for
positive diffusivity.

The density and flux refer to the selected neutral species as a whole,
without resolving its internal states; no sum over different neutral species
is implied. This distinguishes the coefficient from the [poloidal neutral
internal-state diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_diffusion_coefficient),
which applies to a specified internal state. This quantity describes
diffusive particle transport, not convective particle transport or energy
diffusion. Its directional counterpart, [parallel neutral particle
diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_diffusivity), instead resolves
transport along the magnetic field.

items.name: perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species in one internal state is
their mean normal kinetic stress in the two directions perpendicular to the
local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals in a specified internal quantum or
excitation state is the mean of the two normal kinetic stresses
perpendicular to the local magnetic field. It describes the transverse
stress of that nonthermal population without requiring equality with its
field-parallel stress.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse projection of the
pressure tensor:

$$
p_{\perp,0,a}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{1}{2}\left[\operatorname{tr}\mathsf{P}_{0,a}^{\mathrm{fast}} - \hat{b}\cdot\mathsf{P}_{0,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{b}\right]
$$

where $p_{\perp,0,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular pressure,
$\mathsf{P}_{0,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor of the
selected suprathermal neutral population, the subscript $0$ denotes the
selected neutral species, $a$ labels its internal state, and
$\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace. The superscript
$\mathrm{fast}$ denotes the suprathermal population. The unit vector
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ follows the nonzero local magnetic field
$\mathbf{B}$.

This is a partial pressure for one neutral species and one internal state,
not a sum over species or internal states. It excludes thermal-neutral and
charged-particle contributions. The internal-state label selects the
particles contributing translational kinetic stress; their internal
excitation energy is not itself a pressure contribution.

This quantity is the field-perpendicular component of the [suprathermal
neutral internal-state
pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure), rather than
its isotropic trace pressure. Together with the [parallel fast-neutral
internal-state
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure), it specifies
the gyrotropic part of the selected population's pressure tensor.

items.name: ratio_of_parallel_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description:
Ratio of the density-weighted mean field-aligned bulk velocity of an ion
species over all ionization charge states to the local total magnetic-field
magnitude.
items.documentation:
Ratio of the density-weighted mean field-parallel bulk velocity of one ion
species over all its ionization charge states to the local total
magnetic-field magnitude. It expresses signed field-aligned motion scaled by
the inverse total-field strength.

For ion species $i$, the ratio is defined by

$$
K_{i,\parallel} = \frac{v_{i,\parallel}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $K_{i,\parallel}$ is this ratio, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the [parallel
ion velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity), and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local
total magnetic-field vector. The subscript $\parallel$ denotes projection
parallel to $\mathbf{B}$, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is the [magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude). The index $i$ identifies the ion
species.

For each ion species, $v_{i,\parallel}$ is the density-weighted mean over
all ionization charge states, formed from the field-parallel components of
the [charge-state-resolved ion velocities](name:ion_charge_state_velocity).
This is a mean, not a sum or a single-charge-state value; it excludes other
ion species and neutral particles. The numerator and denominator refer to
the same local position, with no spatial aggregation. The ratio is defined
only where the local total magnetic-field magnitude is nonzero.

Multiplying the ratio by the local [magnetic-field
magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude) recovers the [parallel ion
velocity](name:parallel_ion_velocity), which is the parallel component of
the [ion velocity](name:ion_velocity). Unlike the [parallel plasma
velocity-to-field
ratio](name:ratio_of_parallel_plasma_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude),
this quantity describes one ion species rather than the aggregate plasma
center-of-mass motion.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted mean ion bulk velocity
has a component in the direction of the local total magnetic-field vector.

$$a/b$$

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field
items.description:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the toroidal component of the
complex linear-MHD magnetic-field perturbation carried by the
confined-plasma response about equilibrium.
items.documentation:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic field is the toroidal component of the
complex linear-MHD eigenfunction, or corresponding real perturbation, of the
magnetic-field deviation carried by the confined-plasma response about an
equilibrium field. It is the toroidal projection of the [perturbed plasma
magnetic field](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field) and excludes
separately represented externally imposed vacuum perturbations.

The toroidal component is defined by

$$
\delta B_{\mathrm{pl},\phi}(\mathbf{x},t) = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\delta B_{\mathrm{pl},\phi}$ is the toroidal component,
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the plasma-response perturbation,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the
toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with
oriented basis
$(\hat{\mathbf{R}},\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}},\hat{\mathbf{Z}})$. Here $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The response field is
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{pl}}=\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_0-\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$,
where $\mathbf{B}$ is total field, $\mathbf{B}_0$ is equilibrium field, and
$\delta\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is a separately represented vacuum
perturbation. For a specified toroidal Fourier harmonic, the [real
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part) and
[imaginary
part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) are
phase components of this same toroidal quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the corresponding real-valued perturbation
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: neutral_energy_flux
items.description:
Neutral energy flux is the signed thermal energy transported across an
oriented surface per unit area and time by neutral atoms and molecules,
summed over species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral energy flux is the net thermal-energy transport carried by neutral
atoms and molecules across an oriented surface per unit area and time. It
represents a surface-normal projection of the full neutral energy-flux
vector, without selecting a particular geometrical or magnetic-field
direction.

Its defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{W,0} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,0}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n} = \frac{d\dot W_{0,\mathrm{net}}}{dA}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,0}$ is the signed neutral thermal-energy flux through the
surface, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,0}$ is the corresponding energy-flux
vector, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface unit normal, $\dot
W_{0,\mathrm{net}}$ is the net neutral thermal-energy transfer rate across
that surface, and $dA$ is an infinitesimal surface area.

Contributions are summed over the included neutral species and their
internal states; [neutral-species energy
flux](name:neutral_species_energy_flux) resolves the species contributions.
The total includes neutral thermal-energy transport without restriction to
diffusion and excludes energy carried by charged particles or radiation. It
is neither an area-integrated power nor the magnitude or sum of geometrical
vector components. Unlike [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux), it expresses energy transport rather than
particle-number transport.

The [radial neutral energy flux](name:radial_neutral_energy_flux) is the
projection along increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical
height. The [parallel neutral energy
flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux) is the projection along the local
magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral thermal energy crosses the oriented
surface in the direction of its chosen unit normal.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current
items.description:
Toroidal magnetic flux at the halo boundary due to poloidal current is the
signed flux through the poloidal cross-section bounded by the outermost
halo-region flux surface, retaining only the toroidal magnetic-field
contribution generated by poloidal halo current. It excludes contributions
from all other current systems.
items.documentation:
Toroidal magnetic flux at the halo boundary due to poloidal current is the
signed toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section bounded by
the outermost halo-region flux surface. It contains only the magnetic-field
contribution generated by the
[poloidal_halo_current](name:poloidal_halo_current), the poloidal component
of halo current.

Let $S_h$ be the area enclosed by the halo-boundary contour in a plane of
constant toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise
when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. With the
oriented surface element $d\mathbf{S}=+\hat{\phi}\,dA$, the flux is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},h}^{(\mathrm{pol})} = \int_{S_h} \mathbf{B}_h^{(\mathrm{pol})}\cdot d\mathbf{S} = \int_{S_h} B_{\phi,h}^{(\mathrm{pol})}\,dA
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},h}^{(\mathrm{pol})}$ denotes this quantity,
$\mathbf{B}_h^{(\mathrm{pol})}$ is the magnetic-field contribution from
poloidal halo current, $B_{\phi,h}^{(\mathrm{pol})}$ is its component along
$+\hat{\phi}$ in tesla, $d\mathbf{S}$ is the oriented surface element in
square meters, and $dA$ is the corresponding scalar area element in square
meters.

This quantity is the poloidal-current source component of
[toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary),
which includes all magnetic-field sources. It excludes toroidal flux
contributions generated by any current other than poloidal halo current and
is distinct from
[poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_halo_boundary),
which concerns poloidal magnetic flux at the same halo boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic-field contribution generated by
the poloidal halo current crosses $S_h$ in the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction of
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: runaway_electron_particle_flux
items.description:
Directed number flow of runaway electrons across an oriented surface per
unit area and time, including convective, diffusive, drift, and turbulent
transport.
items.documentation:
Runaway-electron particle flux quantifies the directed transport of runaway
electrons across an oriented reference surface. It is the
runaway-electron-specific realization of particle_flux, with the electron
population restricted to the runaway regime.

For a fluid description, the particle flux vector is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE}} = n_{\mathrm{RE}}\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{RE}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron number density and
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is their mean velocity. The scalar flux through
an oriented surface is $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{RE}}\cdot\hat{n}$,
where $\hat{n}$ is the chosen unit surface normal; kinetically, the vector
is the first velocity moment of the runaway-electron distribution.

This parent quantity is not restricted to a particular direction or
projection. The [perpendicular runaway-electron particle
flux](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_particle_flux) is its cross-field
specialization obtained by projecting the vector onto the outward magnetic
flux-surface normal.

Sign convention: Positive when runaway electrons flow in the direction of
the outward surface normal, away from the enclosed plasma volume.

items.name: helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous equivalent-electron helium-3 source rate delivered to the
plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected helium-3 atom
contributes two equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The helium-3 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the
instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-3 is admitted to the plasma
vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count
rate. Each helium-3 atom contributes two equivalent-electron counts because
helium has atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{He}} = 2$.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}$ is the helium-3
equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection,
$\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}$ is the raw neutral helium-3 atomic
delivery rate due to gas injection, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}$ is the atomic
number of helium.

This quantity is isotope-specific: it applies only to neutral helium-3 gas
admitted through gas injection and is aggregated over all gas-injection
paths feeding the plasma vessel. It excludes helium-4 and other injected
species, particle sources not due to gas injection, and raw gas-particle
accounting represented by the gas particle source rate over vessel due to
gas injection.

It is the time derivative of the [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection) under the
same equivalent-electron weighting. Summing species-specific
equivalent-electron source rates over active injected species gives the
[source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).
The [helium-4 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same
helium atomic-number weighting but applies to a different isotope, whereas
the [hydrogen source rate due to gas
injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) differs through
the hydrogen atomic number.

Sign convention: Positive when helium-3 gas is delivered into the plasma
vessel, increasing the helium-3 equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density
items.description:
Volumetric rate of direct coherent-wave energy absorption by fast ions of a
specified species and charge state or bundle, resolved by toroidal mode. It
is expressed either locally or as an average over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Mode-resolved fast-ion charge-state power density is the rate per physical
volume at which coherent-wave energy is absorbed directly by fast ions of a
specified species and charge state or charge-state bundle. The contribution
from each toroidal mode is resolved separately, and the spatial quantity may
be local or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.

The local absorbed power density for a toroidal mode is defined by

$$
p_{s,q}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs},s,q}^{(n_\phi)}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{s,q}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local power density absorbed
from mode $n_\phi$, $P_{\mathrm{abs},s,q}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the power absorbed
from that mode by the specified fast-ion population within volume $V$, $V$
is physical volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position. The index $s$
identifies the ion species, $q$ identifies its charge state or charge-state
bundle, and $n_\phi$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number. The
flux-surface-averaged form is the average of the local quantity over the
corresponding magnetic flux surface.

The recipient population is the fast-ion population of the specified species
