and charge state or bundle; different species are not combined. A bundle
includes the sum over its constituent charge states, while separate toroidal
modes remain resolved. The quantity excludes absorption by thermal ions and
electrons, as well as subsequent collisional redistribution of absorbed
energy. It represents a mode's absorbed-power contribution, not a Fourier
coefficient of the spatial power-density field.

At fixed mode, summing over all charge states of the same species gives the
[per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density). Summing over
toroidal modes and integrating over the plasma volume gives the [fast-ion
charge-state absorbed wave
power](name:fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power) for the specified
species and charge state or bundle.

Sign convention: Positive when coherent-wave energy is transferred to the
specified fast-ion population.

items.name: co_passing_power_density
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for the co-passing orbit
population, representing energy transfer to or from particles circulating in
the co-current direction.
items.documentation:
Co-passing power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which kinetic
energy is transferred to or from the co-passing orbit population per unit
physical volume. Co-passing particles are passing particles that circulate
continuously in the co-current direction.

For a flux surface labeled by poloidal magnetic flux $psi$, it is defined as

$$
p_{E,\mathrm{co}}(\psi)=\left\langle\frac{dE_{\mathrm{co}}}{dt\,dV}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the kinetic energy of the co-passing population,
$t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and the angle brackets denote a
flux-surface average. Positive values denote net energy gain by this
population; negative values denote net energy loss. Wave-particle
interactions, collisions, and particle sources may contribute. The related
[counter-passing power density](name:counter_passing_power_density) applies
the same energy-transfer definition to the oppositely circulating orbit
class, while power density is the unqualified parent quantity.

items.name: vertical_total_current_density
items.description:
Vertical total current density is the net conventional electric-charge flux
per unit area along the toroidal symmetry axis, summed algebraically over
all included contributions.
items.documentation:
Vertical total current density is the signed projection of the total
electric-current-density vector along the toroidal symmetry axis. It
represents net local charge transport in the vertical direction.

The projection and algebraic aggregation are defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{tot},Z} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \sum_a \mathbf{j}_a\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{tot},Z}$ is the vertical total current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total current-density vector,
$\mathbf{j}_a$ is an included current-density contribution, and $a$ labels
contributions in the decomposition of the total. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ points along increasing vertical height in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In the edge plasma, all included contributions are summed algebraically, so
oppositely directed contributions can cancel. The quantity is not species-
or mechanism-resolved, and it is neither a vector magnitude, a surface
average, nor an area-integrated current.

This quantity specializes [total current
density](name:total_current_density) by fixing its common signed projection
basis to the vertical direction. It is a component of [current
density](name:current_density), distinct from [radial total current
density](name:radial_total_current_density), which describes charge
transport along increasing major radius, and [toroidal total current
density](name:toroidal_total_current_density), which describes transport
around the symmetry axis.

Sign convention: Positive when net conventional electric charge flows in the
direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: volume_averaged_carbon_density
items.description:
Plasma-volume mean of the total number density of elemental carbon, summed
over neutral carbon and all ionic charge states through fully stripped C6+.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged carbon density is the plasma-volume mean of the total number
density of elemental carbon, encompassing neutral carbon atoms and all ionic
charge states from singly ionized C+ through fully stripped C6+.

The volume average of the local [carbon density](name:carbon_density) is
defined by

$$
\langle n_C \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_C(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $n_C(\mathbf{r})$ is the local total carbon number density in
m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the plasma volume in m$^{3}$, $dV$ is the volume element,
and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. The local density includes the sum over
all carbon charge states before the volume average is taken.

This quantity represents a volume average over the specified plasma volume
and is distinct from [line-averaged carbon
density](name:line_averaged_carbon_density), which averages along a plasma
chord.

items.name: incident_ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall
items.description:
Kinetic-energy power delivered per unit wall area by ions in one specified
charge state as they cross the sheath and strike the wall.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the incident kinetic-energy power flux delivered to a wall
surface by ions belonging to one specified ion charge state. It represents
the kinetic energy carried by those ions after traversing the sheath and
arriving at the wall.

At a wall point, the incident kinetic-energy flux is defined by

$$
q^{\mathrm{kin}}_{s,\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s\lvert\mathbf{v}\rvert^2(\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $q^{\mathrm{kin}}_{s,\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident kinetic-energy
flux, $s$ identifies the specified ion charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of
that ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is the ion velocity at the wall,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma toward the
wall, $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of that charge state,
and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integration condition
selects ions moving toward the wall.

The quantity applies locally to the wall surface and is specific to one ion
charge state; it is not summed over ionization states or ion species. It
includes kinetic energy only and excludes neutral-particle energy, radiative
energy, recombination energy, and other non-kinetic contributions.

Summing the charge-state-resolved contributions gives the corresponding
all-ion quantity [ion kinetic energy flux at
wall](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall), while [ion charge state
particle flux at wall](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_at_wall) counts
arriving ions rather than weighting them by kinetic energy. It is distinct
from [total incident neutral energy flux at
wall](name:total_incident_neutral_energy_flux_at_wall), which concerns
neutral particles.

items.name: fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Local net rate at which Coulomb collisions change the kinetic-energy density
of a fast-particle population, including all guiding-center orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle collisional power density is the local rate at which Coulomb
collisions change the kinetic-energy density of a designated nonthermal
particle population. It is a signed collisional source or sink, not the
stored kinetic-energy density or the power transferred to the bulk thermal
population.

The defining relation is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision
operator:

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{a\in\mathrm{fast}} \sum_b \int \mathcal{E}_a(\mathbf{v})\, C_{ab}[f_a,f_b](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-particle collisional
power density at position $\mathbf{x}$, $a$ labels species included in the
designated fast population, $b$ labels the charged collision partners
included in the exchange, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and
$\mathcal{E}_a$ is the kinetic energy of a particle of species $a$. The
functions $f_a$ and $f_b$ are the corresponding phase-space number
distributions, and $C_{ab}$ gives the collisional time derivative of $f_a$
caused by interactions with $b$. The integral covers the full velocity
space, with $d^3v$ denoting its volume element.

The quantity includes all guiding-center orbit classes and does not select a
particular fast-particle species or collision partner. An electron-partner
contribution describes energy exchange from electrons to the fast
population; it does not imply that the receiving fast particles are
electrons. This is a local quantity, not a flux-surface average or a
volume-integrated power.

The [co-passing
contribution](name:co_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions)
and [counter-passing
contribution](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_power_density_due_to_collisions),
together with the trapped-orbit contribution, sum to this orbit-unrestricted
quantity when those classes partition the fast-particle phase space.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the
kinetic-energy density of the designated fast-particle population.

items.name: inner_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak
items.description:
Dimensionless inward extent of the hard X-ray emissivity peak from its
maximum to the inner half-maximum point in normalized toroidal flux.
items.documentation:
The inner half-width is the inward extent of the hard X-ray emissivity peak
produced by fast electrons, measured along the normalized toroidal flux
coordinate. It is the distance from the peak maximum toward the magnetic
axis to the point where the emissivity falls to half its peak value.

$$
w_{\mathrm{in}} = \rho_{\mathrm{peak}} - \rho_{\mathrm{half,in}}, \qquad \varepsilon_X(\rho_{\mathrm{half,in}}) = \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_X(\rho_{\mathrm{peak}})
$$

where $w_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the inner half-width, $\rho$ is the normalized
toroidal flux coordinate increasing outward from the magnetic axis, and
$\varepsilon_X(\rho)$ is the hard X-ray emissivity as a function of that
coordinate. The subscript $\mathrm{peak}$ denotes the emissivity maximum,
and $\mathrm{half,in}$ denotes the inward half-maximum location.

This quantity applies only to the side of the peak toward the magnetic axis.
It is a geometric width, not an emissivity value, integrated emission, or
average, and is distinct from the corresponding outward half-width. When
both sides are defined, the full peak width is the sum of the inward and
outward half-widths.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser
items.description:
Major-radius location of the Thomson-scattering laser endpoint, measured as
perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of a Thomson-scattering laser is the major-radius
position of its laser-beam endpoint, measured from the toroidal symmetry
axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
R_{\mathrm{end}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{end}}^2+y_{\mathrm{end}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{end}}$ is the endpoint major-radius coordinate, and
$x_{\mathrm{end}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{end}}$ are the endpoint coordinates along
the two horizontal axes of the right-handed Cartesian basis
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{z}$ aligned with the vertical
direction $\hat{Z}$.

This quantity applies to one laser endpoint and is a geometric point
coordinate, not a path average, scattering-volume coordinate, beam
attribute, or plasma-population quantity. It is neither summed nor averaged
over lasers, endpoints, or plasma regions.

It is the Thomson-scattering-laser-specific realization of [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), providing the $R$ coordinate of the
endpoint. It is distinct from the [toroidal coordinate of the
Thomson-scattering
laser](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_thomson_scattering_laser), which
specifies the endpoint's toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_flux_surface
items.description:
Toroidal magnetic field at a flux surface is the signed component of the
equilibrium magnetic-field vector along the φ direction of the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame at a specified point on a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Toroidal magnetic field at a flux surface is the coefficient $B_\phi$
multiplying $\hat{\phi}$ in the cylindrical decomposition of the equilibrium
magnetic-field vector at a point on a selected magnetic flux surface. The
direction $\hat{\phi}$ belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ basis, where $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$.

The component is the signed scalar projection onto the toroidal basis
vector:

$$
B_\phi(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the point on the selected magnetic flux surface and
$\mathbf{B}$ is the equilibrium magnetic-field vector.

This is the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ toroidal component, not the poloidal
magnetic field at a flux surface, radial magnetic field at a flux surface,
vertical magnetic field at a flux surface, or magnetic-field magnitude at a
flux surface. The surface locus is specified independently, for example by
the [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux
surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface); this quantity is not
the flux label itself.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic-field vector component is in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: ion_momentum_source_rate
items.description:
Ion momentum source rate is a scalar rate coefficient for proportional
source, sink, or transfer terms in an ion momentum balance. Its population
scope is ions, while child names may add qualifiers such as an implicit
treatment; the parent does not choose a component, projection, isotope, or
charge state.
items.documentation:
Ion momentum source rate is a scalar coefficient that parameterizes a
source, sink, or transfer term proportional to an ion momentum quantity in
an ion momentum-balance equation. Its population scope is ions, not
electrons, neutrals, or a species-free momentum balance.

For a proportional contribution to an ion momentum source term, the defining
relation is

$$
S_{M_i}^{(\gamma)} = \gamma_i M_i
$$

where $\gamma_i$ is the ion momentum source rate, $M_i$ is the associated
ion momentum quantity for the ion population under consideration, and
$S_{M_i}^{(\gamma)}$ is the corresponding proportional contribution to the
ion momentum source term.

This quantity is the rate coefficient itself, not the ion momentum, the full
source term, a force density, or a torque. The parent name does not select a
spatial component, coordinate direction, flux-surface projection, explicit
or implicit numerical treatment, isotope, or charge state; those
distinctions require more specific names.

The [implicit ion momentum source
rate](name:implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is an implicit-treatment
specialization of this ion parent, used when the proportional source or sink
contribution is represented implicitly. Source contributions that are not
proportional to the associated ion momentum quantity are outside this
rate-coefficient definition.

Sign convention: Positive when the proportional source term has the same
sign as, or acts in the same direction as, the associated ion momentum
quantity.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of deuterium ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux
surface, summed over all deuterium ion charge states and excluding neutral
deuterium.
items.documentation:
Number density of deuterium

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{D}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{D}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{D}}\rangle$ is the averaged deuterium-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{D}}$ is the local deuterium-ion number density, $S$ is
the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is
the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity is summed over all deuterium ion charge states. It is not a
local point value, a volume average, or a density that includes neutral
deuterium.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [deuterium ion
density at the plasma boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary),
replacing the pointwise value with inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient weighting.
It follows the same species-resolved averaging pattern as the
[flux-surface-averaged xenon density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary), with
deuterium ions as the selected population.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient that scales the
collisionless free-streaming bound component-by-component, capping flux
magnitude while preserving its sign.
items.documentation:
The ion momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for
gradient-driven momentum transport, providing one limiter factor for each
selected spatial transport component. It is the ion specialization of
[momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
scaling the collisionless free-streaming bound while preserving the
direction supplied by the underlying diffusive closure.

For each selected component, the limited momentum-flux density is defined by
the harmonic-mean closure:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\alpha_m$ is the momentum-flux limiter coefficient,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming reference
momentum-flux density, $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive
momentum-flux estimate, and $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the resulting limited
flux density.

The shared quantity spans parallel, poloidal, and radial ion components;
[parallel ion momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and
[poloidal ion momentum-flux limiter
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) are
concrete instances. It applies to momentum flux rather than particle, heat,
or energy flux, and the coefficient is non-negative.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal component of deuterium ion bulk velocity at the magnetic axis,
density-weighted over all deuterium ionization states.
items.documentation:
The deuterium ion velocity at the magnetic axis is the density-weighted mean
flow component along the toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It describes ion motion at the magnetic-axis location
and excludes neutral deuterium.

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{D}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})=\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{D},q}v_{\phi,\mathrm{D},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{D},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes the included deuterium ion charge states,
$n_{\mathrm{D},q}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$,
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{D},q}$ is its toroidal velocity component in m s$^{-1}$,
and $(R_{\mathrm{axis}},Z_{\mathrm{axis}})$ are the major-radius and
vertical coordinates of the magnetic axis. The charge-state weighting
distinguishes this species quantity from the all-ion [toroidal ion
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), while the magnetic-axis locus
distinguishes it from [toroidal deuterium velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the deuterium ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, namely $+\hat{\phi}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Vector magnetic-flux contribution of the pressure-gradient-driven
diamagnetic response in a plasma equilibrium, defined relative to the
corresponding reference magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The diamagnetic magnetic-flux contribution is the vector magnetic flux
associated with the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic response in a
plasma equilibrium, measured relative to a corresponding reference field
without that response.

For an integration surface $S$, the contribution is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\mathrm{dia}} = \int_S \Delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}\,dS
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic magnetic-flux
vector, $\Delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the equilibrium magnetic-field
difference attributable to the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic
response, and $dS$ is the scalar surface-area element on $S$.

This quantity applies to the plasma equilibrium as a whole at the surface
used to define the magnetic flux. It retains the vector component
information and the aggregation over the selected surface; it is not
restricted to a single axis projection, species, normalization, or spatial
region.

The reference-field subtraction excludes magnetic flux already present
without the diamagnetic response and distinguishes this contribution from
the total equilibrium magnetic flux. The [toroidal magnetic flux due to
diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is
the toroidal component of this general vector quantity.

Components are resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved magnetic-flux component points
along the corresponding positive basis direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame; the toroidal component is positive toward
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species in a specified internal
quantum or excitation state is their kinetic normal stress along the local
magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species in a specified internal
quantum or excitation state is the field-parallel component of their kinetic
pressure tensor. It describes directional translational stress without
requiring an isotropic velocity distribution.

The parallel component is defined by projection onto the local
magnetic-field direction:

$$
p_{0,s,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf P_{0,s,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $p_{0,s,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the state-resolved parallel
fast-neutral pressure, $\mathbf P_{0,s,a}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
corresponding kinetic pressure-tensor contribution, $0$ denotes electrical
neutrality, $s$ labels the neutral species, and $a$ labels its internal
quantum or excitation state. The superscript $\mathrm{fast}$ selects the
suprathermal population. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf
B|$ follows the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, which must be nonzero to
define this projection.

This quantity includes only the selected species, internal state, and
suprathermal population. It excludes thermal-neutral pressure,
charged-particle pressure, and transverse pressure components.
Internal-state resolution distinguishes neutral excitation states, not ionic
charge states; internal excitation energy is not itself translational
pressure.

Summing the state-resolved pressure contributions over all internal states
gives the [parallel fast-neutral
pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_pressure) of that species. This
aggregation is an additive sum, not a density-weighted mean. The quantity
retains the species and state selection of [suprathermal neutral
internal-state pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure)
while explicitly selecting its field-parallel component.

items.name: current_due_to_ion_cyclotron_current_drive
items.description:
Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by ion-cyclotron wave
absorption and integrated over the plasma cross-section.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net plasma current driven by ion-cyclotron
wave–particle interactions, excluding inductive and non-wave current
contributions. It represents the toroidal component of the current generated
by the absorbed ion-cyclotron power.

The current is obtained by integrating the driven toroidal current density
over the plasma cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{ICCD}} = \int_A j_{\phi,\mathrm{ICCD}}\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{ICCD}}$ is the driven current, $j_{\phi,\mathrm{ICCD}}$ is
the ion-cyclotron-driven toroidal current density in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $A$ is the plasma cross-sectional
area. The quantity is a net current, so oppositely directed local
contributions are algebraically summed. It is a source-specific component of
[current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive](name:current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive)
and is distinct from
[current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive).

Sign convention: Positive when the driven current flows in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity
items.description:
Radial component of the effective convective velocity used for ion particle
transport in the edge plasma, taken along increasing major radius R in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It represents collective
particle-transport advection and is distinct from the ion fluid velocity.
items.documentation:
Radial component of the effective convective velocity used for ion particle
transport is the scalar transport velocity whose multiplication by ion
particle density gives the advective part of the ion particle flux in the
radial direction. For this quantity, the radial direction is the
major-radius direction $\hat R$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The defining relation for the radial convective contribution to the ion
particle flux is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_i v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective ion particle
flux, $n_i$ is the ion particle density, and $v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is
the radial ion particle convection velocity.

The quantity applies to collective ion particle transport in the edge plasma
and to the ion species as a whole. Because velocity is an intensive
per-particle field, the species-level ion value is the density-weighted mean
over all ion charge states; if $q$ indexes ion charge state,
$v_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convection velocity of charge
state $q$, and $n_{i,q}$ is its particle density, then
$v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = (\sum_q n_{i,q}
v_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{conv}})/(\sum_q n_{i,q})$.

This is an effective transport coefficient, not the ion fluid velocity, not
an individual charge-state flow velocity, and not the diffusive contribution
to the radial particle flux. A flux-surface-normal convection velocity is a
different projection; it coincides with this radial component only where the
flux-surface normal is parallel to $\hat R$.

The direction-complement and population-resolved sibling [parallel ion
charge-state convection
velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) describes the
magnetic-field-parallel convective velocity for one ion charge state. This
quantity instead describes the radial component for the
charge-state-aggregated ion population.

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity is directed toward increasing
major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_filter_window
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the filter-window center, giving its signed height
relative to the machine midplane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, this quantity is the
vertical coordinate of the filter-window center, with zero at the machine
midplane. The basis $(\hat{\mathbf{R}}, \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}},
\hat{\mathbf{Z}})$ is right-handed; $R$ is major radius from the machine
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is the projection of the center's position vector onto the
vertical direction:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

Here $Z$ is the filter-window center's vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}$ is
its position vector relative to the frame origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is
the unit vector parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis in the positive $Z$
direction.

This quantity specifies the location of one geometric center point of the
filter window; it is not a surface-averaged coordinate, the window's
vertical extent or orientation, or a coordinate along a filter-local axis.

Together with the [radial coordinate of the filter
window](name:radial_coordinate_of_filter_window) and [toroidal coordinate of
the filter window](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_filter_window), it specifies
the spatial location of the same center. The [vertical coordinate of an
aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture) and [vertical coordinate of
a diagnostic aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture)
refer to different component centers and are not substitutes for this
quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the filter-window center lies above the
machine midplane, in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: ion_energy
items.description:
Ion energy is the aggregate energy attributed to an ion population in a
specified plasma region. As a parent quantity, it does not by itself specify
thermal, fast-ion, suprathermal, bulk-flow, or internal-energy content;
those distinctions are supplied by child names.
items.documentation:
Ion energy is the aggregate energy attributed to an ion population in a
specified plasma region. It is the parent concept for extensive ion-energy
quantities whose child names specify the included ion population and the
energy component being counted.

The scope is the ion contribution to plasma energy: electron and
neutral-particle energies are outside this quantity. Because this is an
extensive quantity, contributions from the included ion species and charge
states are summed over the populations included by the specific ion-energy
definition.

This parent quantity must not be read as specifically thermal, random
translational, fast-ion, suprathermal, internal, or directed bulk-flow
energy. Those component distinctions belong to more specific names; for
example, [thermal ion energy](name:thermal_ion_energy) is the specialization
for the volume-integrated internal energy of the thermal-ion ensemble and
carries its own exclusions of electron, fast-ion, and suprathermal
contributions.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity
items.description:
Parallel component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Parallel component of the effective convective velocity used for particle
transport of a specified ion charge state in an edge plasma. It is the
field-aligned component of the vector defined by [ion charge-state
convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) for that
charge-state population.

The parallel component is defined by projection onto the local
magnetic-field direction:

$$
v_{s,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $v_{s,\parallel}$ is this parallel ion charge-state convection
velocity, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the [ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) vector for ion charge
state $s$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

The scope is charge-state resolved: $s$ denotes one specified ion charge
state in the edge plasma, with no summation over charge states and no
density-weighted mean over all charge states. The quantity is an effective
particle-transport coefficient for that charge state, including the
applicable thermal and nonthermal populations represented by the
charge-state particle population.

It is distinct from the parallel ion fluid velocity or kinetic bulk
velocity: it is the coefficient multiplying charge-state number density in
convective particle transport and need not equal a moment of the particle
velocity distribution. The total particle flux may also contain diffusive
transport, which is excluded from this convective velocity.

The field-aligned convective particle-flux component
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ satisfies
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}} = n_s v_{s,\parallel}$, where
$\Gamma_{s,\parallel,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-aligned convective
particle-flux component and $n_s$ is the number density of ion charge state
$s$. Together with directional components such as the [poloidal ion
charge-state convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) and [radial
ion charge-state convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity), it is a
projection of the same parent vector; the parallel direction is
field-aligned and is not the poloidal tangent direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection velocity is directed
along the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$.

items.name: parallel_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description:
Signed plasma flow along the local magnetic field, equal to the
mass-density-weighted mean of the field-parallel velocities of all
constituent species.
items.documentation:
The parallel center-of-mass velocity is the component of the multicomponent
plasma's [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) along the
local magnetic field. It retains the mass-density weighting of the full
barycentric velocity.

The defining projection is

$$
V_{\mathrm{cm},\parallel} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s\,\mathbf{V}_s\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{\sum_s \rho_s}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{cm},\parallel}$ is the parallel center-of-mass velocity,
$\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is the full center-of-mass velocity vector, $s$
indexes constituent species, $\rho_s$ is each species' mass density,
$\mathbf{V}_s$ is its mean velocity, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit
vector directed along the local magnetic field.

The sum includes all species in the plasma mixture, not only ions. This is a
local mass-density-weighted mean, not a particle-number-weighted mean or an
unweighted sum of species velocities. The definition requires nonzero total
mass density and a nonzero magnetic field.

The [bulk center-of-mass velocity](name:bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the
corresponding full vector; this projection excludes its perpendicular
components and is distinct from its speed.

Sign convention: Positive when the center-of-mass flow component points
along the local magnetic field.

items.name: vertical_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element
items.description:
Radius of curvature of an optical element's beam-entry front surface along
the local second tangential direction (X2, the optical-element vertical
direction) in the right-handed local optical-element frame (X1, X2, z).
items.documentation:
Radius of curvature of an optical element's beam-entry front surface along
the local second tangential ($X_2$, optical-element vertical) direction is
the signed radius of the front-surface normal section spanned by $\hat{X}_2$
and $\hat{z}$ in the right-handed local optical-element frame
$(\hat{X}_1,\hat{X}_2,\hat{z})$. The coordinates $x_1$ and $x_2$ lie in the
local tangent plane at the surface vertex, and $z$ is the local
front-surface-normal sag coordinate. This is a radius of curvature, not a
reciprocal curvature.

At the surface vertex, after subtracting planar tilt so that $\partial
z/\partial x_2=0$ there, the signed radius is defined by the second
derivative of the sag in the $X_2$ normal section:

$$
\frac{1}{R_2} = \left.\frac{\partial^2 z}{\partial x_2^2}\right|_{x_2=0}
$$

where $z(x_2)$ is the front-surface sag along $\hat{z}$, $x_2$ is
displacement along $\hat{X}_2$, and $R_2$ is this signed radius; $z$, $x_2$,
and $R_2$ are in meters. For small sag this definition implies
$z(x_2)-z(0)\simeq x_2^2/(2R_2)$ near the vertex, and a flat section is the
limiting case $1/R_2=0$.

For spherical surface models the first- and second-local-tangential radii of
the front surface are equal. For cylindrical, toroidal, or separably curved
surface models they may differ, so this quantity is distinct from the
orthogonal first-local-tangential front-surface quantity
x_front_surface_curvature_of_optical_element and from the rear-surface
quantity
[vertical_back_surface_curvature_of_optical_element](name:vertical_back_surface_curvature_of_optical_element);
[vertical_front_surface_curvature_of_optical_element](name:second_local_tangential_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element)
uses the same second-local-tangential front-surface radius convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the center of curvature of the front surface
in the normal section spanned by $\hat{X}_2$ and $\hat{z}$ lies on the
$+\hat{z}$ side of the local tangent plane.

items.name: energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fick's-law coefficient relating the diffusive thermal energy flux of a
plasma constituent to its local temperature gradient, serving as the
species-agnostic parent abstraction over electron, ion, and neutral
population specializations.
items.documentation:
The energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven thermal
energy transport for any plasma constituent — electrons, ions, or neutrals —
by specifying the proportionality between the diffusive heat flux and the
local temperature gradient in the Fick's-law sense. It is the thermal-energy
channel of the general diffusion_coefficient, which governs particle,
momentum, and energy transport alike, and it is distinct from convective or
$E \times B$ contributions to the total heat flux.

The defining relation for the diffusive energy flux
$\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{diff}$ of a given constituent is:

$$
\mathbf{Q}_\mathrm{diff} = -D_E \, \nabla T
$$

where $D_E$ is the energy diffusion coefficient and $\nabla T$ is the
temperature gradient of that constituent. In a magnetized plasma $D_E$ is
strongly anisotropic; radial cross-field values govern energy confinement
while values along field lines are orders of magnitude larger.

Species-resolved children include
[electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:electron_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
for the electron population and
[ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient)
for the total ion population aggregated over all charge states;
neutral-particle transport is handled by analogous neutral specializations.
The effective diffusivity that combines diffusive and convective
contributions is tracked separately by energy_effective_diffusivity.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_plasma_boundary_gap_reference_point
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the plasma-boundary gap reference point, expressed as
signed height from the coordinate origin in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the plasma-boundary gap reference point specifies its
signed height relative to the coordinate origin in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $Z$ is the reference point's vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}$ is its
position vector relative to the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is
the unit vector along the toroidal symmetry axis in the positive vertical
direction. The coordinates $R$ and $\phi$ denote major radius and toroidal
angle, respectively.

The quantity applies to one reference point, without averaging over the
plasma boundary. It is a point coordinate, not the gap distance or a
vertical clearance between the plasma and the wall. The [vertical coordinate
of the closest wall point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point)
uses the same vertical-axis convention but locates a separately defined
point.

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the coordinate origin
to the reference point has a positive projection onto $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$.

items.name: inner_radius_of_passive_loop
items.description:
Inner radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop
element is the Euclidean distance from the cross-section center to its inner
conducting boundary. It is nonnegative.
items.documentation:
Inner radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop
element is the Euclidean distance, in the $(R,Z)$ plane at fixed toroidal
angle $phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,phi,Z)$ frame, from the
center of the annular conductor cross-section to its inner conducting
boundary. Here $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The inner boundary radius is defined by the poloidal-plane distance from the
cross-section center to the selected inner-boundary point:

$$
r_\mathrm{inner} = \sqrt{(R_i - R_c)^2 + (Z_i - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $(R_c,Z_c)$ is the annular cross-section center and $(R_i,Z_i)$ is the
inner-boundary position in the same fixed-$\phi$ plane; all coordinate
components in the equation are expressed in meters.

This quantity specializes
[radius_of_passive_loop](name:radius_of_passive_loop) to the inner
conducting boundary and complements
[outer_radius_of_passive_loop](name:outer_radius_of_passive_loop). For a
circular annulus, the conductor thickness is the outer radius minus this
inner radius, and [area_of_passive_loop](name:area_of_passive_loop) is
determined by the difference of the squared outer and inner radii. It is a
cross-sectional size, not the loop center's major-radius coordinate or a
signed cylindrical component.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_source
items.description:
Signed rate of toroidal linear-momentum transfer to the total ion population
per unit area, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion momentum source is the signed rate of transfer of
toroidally directed linear momentum to the ion population per unit area. It
is the toroidal projection of the [ion momentum
source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The projection and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
S_{i,\phi} = \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \hat{\phi} = \sum_z S_{i,z,\phi}
$$

where $S_{i,\phi}$ is this toroidal source, $\mathbf{S}_i$ is the ion
momentum-source vector, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing
toroidal angle, and $S_{i,z,\phi}$ is the toroidal source for ionic charge
state $z$. The index $i$ identifies the ion population, and the sum includes
all ionic charge states.

This is a charge-state-summed source, not a source for one selected charge
state; electrons and neutral particles are excluded from the receiving
population. It describes transfer of [linear momentum](name:momentum) to
ions, rather than [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) through a surface. Its
area-normalized linear-momentum transfer is also distinct from [ion torque
density](name:ion_torque_density), which describes angular-momentum transfer
per unit volume.

Sign convention: Positive when the net linear momentum transferred to ions
points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Signed local binormal projection of the density-weighted ion velocity
contribution produced by pressure-gradient diamagnetic drift, averaged over
all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The binormal ion diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed local projection
of the ion population's velocity contribution produced by pressure-gradient
diamagnetic drift. It is a velocity component, not a momentum flux or
particle flux.

$$
v_{i,\mathrm{bin}}^{*} = \mathbf{v}_{i}^{*} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bin}}
$$

Here, $\mathbf{v}_{i}^{*}$ is the vector ion velocity contribution from
diamagnetic drift, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bin}}$ is the designated
positive local binormal unit vector, and $v_{i,\mathrm{bin}}^{*}$ is their
signed projection. The subscript $i$ denotes the ion population and the
superscript $*$ identifies the diamagnetic-drift contribution.

This quantity applies to the ion population with a density-weighted mean
taken over all ionic charge states. It excludes neutral particles and is not
the velocity of one specified ion charge state. The corresponding
charge-state-resolved quantity, such as [perpendicular ion charge-state
diamagnetic-drift
velocity](name:perpendicular_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift),
retains the individual charge-state distinction rather than applying this
aggregation.

The binormal component is one projection of the full ion diamagnetic-drift
velocity. It is distinct from the analogous [toroidal ion diamagnetic-drift
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), which
projects the same charge-state-averaged contribution onto the toroidal
direction, and from parallel or field-normal projections that use different
directions.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion diamagnetic-drift velocity points
along the designated positive local binormal direction.

items.name: lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless lower triangularity shape parameter for a nested magnetic flux
surface, given by the normalized inward radial displacement of its lower
vertical extremum.
items.documentation:
Lower triangularity of a flux surface is the dimensionless triangularity
shape parameter defined at the lower vertical extremum of a nested magnetic
flux surface. It is the normalized inward displacement in major radius $R$
of that lower extremum relative to the magnetic-axis reference.

For the lower vertical extremum, the defining relation is:

$$
\delta_{\mathrm{lower}} = \frac{R_{\mathrm{axis}} - R_{\mathrm{lower}}}{a}
$$

where $\delta_{\mathrm{lower}}$ is lower triangularity, $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$
is the major-radius coordinate of the magnetic axis, $R_{\mathrm{lower}}$ is
the major-radius coordinate of the lower vertical extremum, and $a$ is the
minor radius of the same flux surface. These coordinates are defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius
measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height.

This quantity applies independently to each nested magnetic flux surface and
is a geometrical property of the surface rather than a plasma-population
quantity. It resolves the lower vertical extremum only; it is not averaged
over flux surfaces or combined with the upper extremum. It is distinct from
[lower triangularity of a flux surface
boundary](name:lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary), which describes the
outer plasma boundary rather than an arbitrary nested surface.

It is the lower-extremum branch of [triangularity of a flux
surface](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface), whose parent quantity permits
the relevant upper or lower vertical extremum. The corresponding [upper
triangularity of a flux surface](name:upper_triangularity_of_flux_surface)
uses the upper vertical extremum, while [elongation of a flux
surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface) describes vertical-to-horizontal
shaping rather than triangular displacement.

Sign convention: Positive when the lower vertical extremum lies at smaller
major radius $R$ than the magnetic-axis reference, corresponding to an
inward displacement.

items.name: total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the non-negative total
unweighted rate at which neutral gas particles are injected by gas valves
assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It is not an electron-equivalent
or charge-weighted rate.
items.documentation:
Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the instantaneous total
unweighted source rate of neutral gas particles injected by gas-injection
valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It counts injected
neutral gas particles themselves, not electron-equivalent particles,
charge-weighted particles, or particles produced by later plasma or wall
interactions.

For the set of midplane injection valves, the total rate is the sum of the
individual unweighted valve particle throughputs:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}} \dot{N}_k
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}}$ is the gas source rate at
midplane due to gas injection, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is the set of
gas-injection valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane, and
$\dot{N}_k$ is the unweighted neutral-particle throughput of valve $k$.

The total includes all gas-injection valves in the midplane group and
excludes upper, lower, wall, recycling, pumping, ionization, and transport
contributions. It is not additive with regional gas-source quantities that
use an electron-equivalent or charge-weighted convention. Its time integral
is the corresponding [accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_total_gas_count_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the collisionless
free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density for a specified ion
charge state, applied component-by-component in multi-fluid edge plasma
transport closures.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state momentum coefficient is the charge-state-resolved ion
specialization of
[momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
providing one dimensionless limiter factor per spatial transport direction
for momentum flux attributed to a specific ion charge state in multi-fluid
edge plasma transport closures.

Each vector component $\alpha_s$ bounds the corresponding directional
momentum-flux density through the harmonic-mean combination:

$$
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_s \, \Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux
estimate for charge state $s$, and $\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}} = m_s n_s
v_{\mathrm{th},s}^2$ is the free-streaming reference scale with $m_s$ the
ion mass, $n_s$ the charge-state number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th},s}$ the
thermal speed. When $|\Pi_s^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_s
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm\alpha_s
\Pi_s^{\mathrm{FS}}$; otherwise the diffusive value is recovered unchanged.

The vector components provide separate limiter factors for each spatial
direction; the
[parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
is the scalar projection onto the magnetic-field direction. The
neutral-particle analog is
[neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient).
Each component is intrinsically non-negative.

items.name: viewing_efficiency_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Fraction of locally emitted light collected by a spectrometer channel’s
optical system from each specified region-of-interest point, including
non-pinhole viewing geometries.
items.documentation:
Viewing efficiency is the geometric fraction of radiation emitted locally at
a specified point that is collected by the optical system of a spectrometer
channel. It characterizes spatial light collection for non-pinhole optics,
rather than the probability that a detector registers an incident photon.

For a point at position $mathbf{r}$, the viewing efficiency is defined by

$$
\eta_{\mathrm{view}}(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{collected}}(\mathbf{r})}{\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{local}}(\mathbf{r})}
$$

where $\eta_{\mathrm{view}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the viewing efficiency,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the spatial emission point,
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{collected}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local emission
contribution collected by the optical system, and
$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{local}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the corresponding local
emitted radiation considered by the collection model.

The quantity is evaluated separately at each point defining a region of
interest and is a fraction bounded between zero and one. It represents
spatial collection and is not summed or averaged over the region-of-interest
points. It is not a wavelength-resolved efficiency and excludes
detector-registration probability or other spectral detector response.

Viewing efficiency is related to the optical phase-space acceptance
described by etendue of a spectrometer channel, but it is a pointwise
collection fraction rather than an etendue. It is distinct from [spectral
efficiency of a hard X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector), which is an
energy-dependent photon-registration probability.

items.name: toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions at the last
closed flux surface, resolved along increasing toroidal angle.
items.documentation:
The deuterium toroidal velocity is the local toroidal projection of the
density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of deuterium ions at the plasma
boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It excludes neutral
deuterium and is not a flux-surface average.

$$
v_{D,\phi}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\frac{\sum_{q\in Q_D}n_{D,q}\mathbf{v}_{D,q}}{\sum_{q\in Q_D}n_{D,q}}
$$

Here $Q_D$ is the set of included deuterium ion charge states, $n_{D,q}$ is
the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{D,q}$ is its bulk-flow
velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The local quantity is distinct from the
toroidal flux-surface-averaged deuterium velocity at the plasma boundary and
from the corresponding value at the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the deuterium bulk velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the
krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis, defined as the
density-weighted mean over all krypton ionization states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal component, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, of
the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic axis is the
charge-state-aggregated krypton velocity projected along $\hat{\phi}$. Here
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and
the magnetic axis is the innermost closed-flux-surface locus where the
gradient of [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) vanishes.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity at this locus is defined by
projecting the density-weighted krypton velocity onto the toroidal unit
vector:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Kr},0} =
\left.
\left(
\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}
\right)
\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ionization charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$
is the number density of charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$
is its bulk-flow velocity, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle, and the subscript $0$ denotes evaluation at
the magnetic axis.

This is an intensive species velocity: krypton charge-state velocities are
combined as a density-weighted mean over all ionization states, not as a
sum. It is distinct from flux-surface-averaged toroidal krypton velocity at
the plasma boundary and from local toroidal krypton velocities at the
[internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier) and
[pedestal top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the krypton velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Toroidal component of the oxygen ion bulk velocity, evaluated at the radial
location of the internal transport barrier in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame. For species-level oxygen, this is the density-weighted mean
over all charge states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal component of the oxygen ion bulk velocity at an internal transport
barrier is the component of the oxygen bulk-flow velocity along the toroidal
basis direction at the radial location of the internal transport barrier.
The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

For species-level oxygen, the velocity is the density-weighted mean over all
oxygen charge states:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{O}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}}) = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}(r_{\mathrm{ITB}})}
$$

where $r_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the radial location of the internal transport
barrier, $q$ indexes oxygen charge states, $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of oxygen charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is
its bulk velocity, and $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle.

This quantity is a local toroidal component at the
internal-transport-barrier locus, not a flux-surface average or a boundary
value. Same-locus species counterparts include [toroidal carbon velocity at
internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
[toroidal xenon velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_xenon_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier),
[toroidal nitrogen velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier), and
[toroidal deuterium velocity at internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier);
the same-species boundary counterpart is toroidal flux-surface-averaged
oxygen velocity at plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted oxygen ion bulk flow is
in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough
items.description:
Toroidal component of torque carried away by neutral beam particles that
traverse the plasma without ionization, representing angular momentum not
transferred to the plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal shinethrough torque is the component of angular-momentum loss
carried away by neutral beam particles that remain neutral while traversing
the plasma and exit without transferring their momentum to the plasma. It is
the toroidal component of the parent [torque due to neutral beam
shinethrough](name:torque_due_to_neutral_beam_shinethrough).

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{sh}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{sh}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the total shinethrough torque
vector and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity includes only
angular momentum carried away by non-ionized beam neutrals; it excludes
momentum deposited by neutrals that ionize and is distinct from local
[toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density) and [toroidal
neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density).

Sign convention: Positive when $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Convection velocity for cross-flux-surface transport of toroidal momentum
carried by one neutral species, aggregated over neutral states. Toroidal
denotes the momentum component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, not velocity direction.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neutral species momentum convection velocity is the
flux-surface-normal convection coefficient that multiplies the toroidal
momentum density carried by neutrals of one chemical species. The toroidal
momentum component is defined along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the coefficient itself is not a
velocity directed along $\hat{\phi}$. It is the toroidal component of the
[neutral species momentum convection
velocity](name:neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity).

The defining relation preserves the total convective flux of toroidal
momentum across a magnetic flux surface:

$$
\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = P_{\phi,a} V_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \sum_{s \in a} P_{\phi,s} V_{\phi,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $a$ denotes one neutral chemical species, $s$ runs over its resolved
neutral states, $P_{\phi,s}$ and $P_{\phi,a}$ are signed toroidal momentum
densities, $V_{\phi,s}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and $V_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ are
state-resolved and species-aggregated convection coefficients, and
$\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the corresponding convective momentum
flux. The state sum excludes other chemical species; this is a local
coefficient, not a flux-surface average. The one-species aggregation
distinguishes it from the broader [toroidal neutral momentum convection
velocity](name:toroidal_neutral_momentum_convection_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when $\Gamma_{\phi,a}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ and
$P_{\phi,a}$ have the same sign, with positive toroidal momentum directed
toward increasing $\phi$ and positive flux-surface-normal transport directed
toward increasing magnetic flux label.

items.name: turn_count_of_correction_coil
items.description:
Total winding-turn count assigned to one non-axisymmetric correction coil,
including fractional values when the circuit represents partial coil
connections.
items.documentation:
The correction-coil turn count is the total number of winding turns assigned
to one non-axisymmetric coil used for magnetic-field correction. It
represents the coil's winding count rather than a field, current, or
electromagnetic load.

The quantity applies to the selected correction coil and aggregates all
turns assigned to that coil. Fractional values are permitted when the
circuit description represents partial coil connections; they do not
indicate a fractional physical turn in an individual winding.

This un-oriented total winding count is distinct from the signed
equivalent-winding quantity for a passive conducting loop, [effective turn
count of a passive loop](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop), which
weights electromagnetic coupling. Its treatment of fractional connections is
analogous to [turn count of a toroidal field
coil](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_field_coil), while retaining the
correction-coil ownership and non-axisymmetric scope.

items.name: length_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Geometric length of either inclined side of the oblique cross-section of a
passive loop element, including its major and minor sides.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric side length of an oblique or parallelogram
cross-section belonging to a passive loop element. It describes the side
itself rather than an electrical or material property.

For side endpoints with position vectors $\mathbf{r}_1$ and $\mathbf{r}_2$
in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, the
length $\ell$ is defined by

$$
\ell = \|\mathbf{r}_2 - \mathbf{r}_1\|
$$

where $\ell$ is the side length, and $\mathbf{r}_1$ and $\mathbf{r}_2$ are
the endpoint position vectors.

The scope includes both side orientations of the passive loop element's
oblique cross-section: the major-side instance [major length of a passive
loop element](name:major_length_of_passive_loop_element) and the minor-side
instance [minor length of a passive loop
element](name:minor_length_of_passive_loop_element). It excludes the
cross-section thickness measured perpendicular to the element's central
segment, represented separately by [thickness of a passive loop
element](name:thickness_of_passive_loop_element). The length is nonnegative
and is independent of which side orientation is selected.

items.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal flow velocity of ionized nitrogen across its
charge states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge
transport barrier.
items.documentation:
The toroidal nitrogen velocity at the pedestal top is the density-weighted
mean flow of ionized nitrogen ions over all nitrogen charge states at the
core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It describes flow
rather than abundance, which is represented by nitrogen density at the
pedestal top.

For nitrogen charge states $q=1,\ldots,7$, the species velocity is defined
by

$$
v_{\phi,N} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{7} n_q v_{\phi,q}}{\sum_{q=1}^{7} n_q}
$$

where $n_q$ is the number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$ and
$v_{\phi,q}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$, measured in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Neutral nitrogen is excluded.
The pedestal-top value is distinguished from the corresponding [toroidal
nitrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) by its edge-barrier
location.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted velocity points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: gap_at_closest_wall_point
items.description:
Gap at the closest-wall point measures the minimum Euclidean separation
between the plasma separatrix and limiter or wall material.
items.documentation:
Gap at closest wall point

The gap is defined by

$$
g = \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{sep}},\,\mathbf{y}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{pw}}}\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2
$$

where $g$ is the gap, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{sep}}$ is the plasma separatrix,
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{pw}}$ is the combined eligible limiter-or-wall boundary,
$\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{y}$ are physical points on those respective
boundaries, and $\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\|_2$ denotes their Euclidean
separation.

The minimum is taken over all eligible boundary-point pairs, rather than
averaged over the wall or restricted to a major-radius separation. The gap
is nonnegative and vanishes when the boundaries touch.

For identical boundaries, its value equals the [gap at the plasma
boundary](name:gap_at_plasma_boundary). The [vertical coordinate of the
closest-wall point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_closest_wall_point)
specifies the vertical position of the evaluation locus, not its clearance
from the plasma.

items.name: total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred to an ion charge
state by collisions, summing contributions from both thermal and fast ion
sub-populations.
items.documentation:
Total Coulomb-collisional power transferred to ions of a specified species
and charge state, integrated over the plasma volume, aggregating
contributions from both the thermal and fast (non-Maxwellian)
sub-populations.

The total is the sum of its population-resolved components:

$$
P_{\rm coll}^{s,z} = P_{\rm th}^{s,z} + P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}
$$

where $P_{\rm th}^{s,z}$ is the [thermal ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions) and
$P_{\rm fast}^{s,z}$ is the [fast ion charge state power due to
collisions](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions), with $s$
denoting the ion species and $z$ the resolved charge state.

This charge-state-resolved total is distinct from
[ion_power_due_to_collisions](name:ion_power_due_to_collisions), which
aggregates over all charge states and both sub-populations without
charge-state resolution.

Sign convention: Positive when the specified ion charge state is a net
recipient of energy from Coulomb collisions.

items.name: volume_averaged_lithium_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged total number density of lithium ions, summed over all charge
states from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, within the confined plasma
volume.
items.documentation:
This is the volume average of lithium ion number density, summed over all
ionization stages from Li+ through fully stripped Li3+, throughout the
confined plasma. Neutral lithium is excluded. The quantity provides a global
measure of lithium impurity content rather than a local or boundary value.

The volume average is defined as

$$
\overline{n}_{Li} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_{Li}\,dV
$$

where $n_{Li}$ is the local lithium-ion number density, $V_p$ is the
confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is
the physical volume element. Unlike the boundary value flux-surface-averaged
lithium density at the plasma boundary, this quantity averages over the full
confined volume. Its electron-normalized counterpart is the ratio of
volume-averaged lithium density to volume-averaged electron density.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_at_pellet_path_point
items.description:
Azimuthal location of a sampled point along the pellet path in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame about the machine symmetry axis.
Phi increases counterclockwise when viewed from above +Z.
items.documentation:
Azimuthal location of a sampled point along the pellet path is the toroidal
coordinate $\phi$ of that point about the machine symmetry axis. It is the
angular component of the point position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,
\phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is the [toroidal angle](name:toroidal_angle), and $Z$
is vertical height.

For the same point projected onto the plane perpendicular to the symmetry
axis, using the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis
with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and $\hat{x}$ defining $\phi=0$, the coordinate is
defined by the oriented azimuth:

$$
\phi = \operatorname{atan2}(y, x)
$$

where $x$ is the coordinate along $\hat{x}$, $y$ is the coordinate along
$\hat{y}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ is the quadrant-resolving azimuth
to the transverse projection of the pellet path point.

The scope is a single geometrical point on the pellet path; the quantity is
point-local and is not averaged or accumulated over any segment of the path.
It is an absolute coordinate, not a toroidal offset from another locus, and
it is not the radial coordinate $R$, the vertical coordinate $Z$, path
length, velocity, or injection direction.

This quantity is the pellet-path-point specialization of [toroidal
angle](name:toroidal_angle). Together with the corresponding $R$ and $Z$
coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it
identifies the point up to the angular periodicity of $\phi$.

Sign convention: Positive when rotation from the $\phi=0$ reference
direction toward the point projection is counterclockwise about the symmetry
axis when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: radial_width_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode
items.description:
Radial width of a neoclassical tearing mode is the full magnetic-island span
along the major-radius direction at a specified time.
items.documentation:
Width of neoclassical tearing mode

The full width is defined by

$$
w(t) = R_+(t) - R_-(t)
$$

where $w$ is the full island width, $t$ is time, and $R_+$ and $R_-$ are the
larger and smaller major-radius coordinates of the opposite
island-separatrix intersections along a major-radius line through the island
center. Major radius $R$ measures distance from the toroidal symmetry axis
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is
toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity describes an individual mode at each time, not a sum over modes
or a temporal average. It is the full width, not the half-width. Its value
at onset is the seed-island width; the same quantity describes the island
size during subsequent evolution.

This width is the island-size variable in the generalized Rutherford
equation. Its [radial-width time
derivative](name:radial_width_time_derivative_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode)
is $dw/dt$, which describes instantaneous island growth or shrinkage.

items.name: total_neutral_particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Wall-integrated neutral-particle number rate emitted into the plasma by
surface-emission processes, with cold, thermal, and fast energy categories
represented separately.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total number rate of neutral particles emitted from
plasma-facing wall surfaces into the adjacent plasma-facing region by
surface-emission processes. It represents the contribution from the selected
neutral population and energy category rather than a local surface flux.

The surface-integrated rate is defined by

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{n,SE}}^{(c)} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} \Gamma_{\mathrm{n,SE}}^{(c)}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{n,SE}}^{(c)}$ is the emitted neutral-particle number
rate, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{n,SE}}^{(c)}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
neutral-particle flux density due to surface emission at wall position
$\mathbf{x}$, $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the emitting wall surface,
$\mathrm{d}A$ is its differential area element, and $c$ identifies the cold,
thermal, or fast neutral energy category.

The aggregation is over the contributing wall surface; “total” does not
imply summation over the cold, thermal, and fast categories, which remain
distinct contributions. The quantity describes particles leaving the wall
and excludes neutral particles incident on the wall, net
incoming-minus-outgoing flux, and volumetric plasma sources.

It is the area integral of [neutral particle flux density due to surface
emission](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission),
whereas [incident neutral particle flux at the
wall](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall) describes particles
arriving at the wall and is not included in this outgoing rate. It is also
distinct from the per-area recombination contribution represented by
[neutral particle flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

items.name: ion_charge_state_power
items.description:
Volume-integrated power transferred from coherent electromagnetic waves to a
selected ion population, with specializations resolving thermal populations
and charge states.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated ion power is the electromagnetic-wave power transferred to
a selected ion population throughout the plasma. It denotes absorbed
transfer to the ions rather than the power incident on, launched by, or
remaining in the wave.

The volume-integrated quantity is defined from the corresponding local
transfer-power density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{ion}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the total power transferred to the selected ion
population, $p_{\mathrm{ion}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local power density
transferred to that population at position $\mathbf{r}$,
$V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential
volume element.

The recipient population is selected by the specialization and may be
resolved by thermal population and charge state; [thermal ion charge-state
power](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power) is the instance for bulk thermal
ions in one specified charge state. The defining aggregation is over plasma
volume, and a charge-state-resolved instance does not implicitly sum over
other charge states.

Power transferred to electrons, power not transferred from the wave, and
wave-system generator or launched power are outside this quantity. It is
distinct from the local power-density quantity, which describes the spatial
distribution before volume integration.

For a matching specialization, integrating [thermal ion charge-state power
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density) over the plasma volume
gives the corresponding volume-integrated power. The broader [ion absorbed
wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) describes coherent-wave power
transferred directly to ion populations, while [total ion
power](name:total_ion_power) is a broader ion-power aggregation that can
include sources or sinks other than coherent electromagnetic-wave
absorption.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description:
Full transverse extent of the rectangular neutral-beam injector ion-source
aperture along the first local tangential axis, defining one aperture
dimension for beam extraction.
items.documentation:
Full transverse extent of the rectangular neutral-beam injector ion-source
aperture along the first local tangential axis is the distance between the
two opposite aperture edges in that object-local tangential direction. It
defines one aperture dimension for beam extraction.

The width is defined by the range of the first local tangential coordinate
over the aperture surface:

$$
w_1 = \max_{\mathbf{r}\in A} \xi_1(\mathbf{r}) - \min_{\mathbf{r}\in A} \xi_1(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential width, $A$ is the rectangular
ion-source aperture surface, $\mathbf{r}$ is a point on that aperture
surface, and $\xi_1$ is the object-local coordinate along the first local
tangential axis.

This quantity applies to rectangular ion-source aperture geometry. It is
distinct from the width along the second local tangential axis and from any
beam envelope, divergence, or focal width away from the ion-source aperture.
As a full width defined by a maximum minus a minimum, it is non-negative:
$w_1 \ge 0$.

items.name: tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of tritium ions at the internal transport barrier,
the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport permits steep radial fuel-ion density gradients to form.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of tritium ions at the internal transport barrier is
the local number density of tritium ions on the flux surface selected as the
barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier is a
confined-plasma region where effective cross-field transport is locally
reduced, allowing steep density gradients to form and persist.

The local tritium-ion density $n_T$ at the ITB reference surface is the
zeroth velocity moment of the charge-state-resolved distribution functions:

$$
n_T(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \sum_Z \int f_{T,Z}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\,d^3v
$$

where $Z$ labels tritium ion charge states, $f_{T,Z}$ is the corresponding
