velocity distribution, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and
$\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ identifies the ITB flux surface in coordinates $(\rho,
\theta, \phi)$. This quantity is summed over all tritium ion charge states
and excludes neutral tritium. It is the tritium-specific counterpart of ion
density at the internal transport barrier and contributes to the
species-agnostic [density at the internal transport
barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

items.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion fluid velocity evaluated at
the magnetic axis, the innermost point of the confined plasma where the
poloidal magnetic flux gradient vanishes.
items.documentation:
The toroidal component of the tungsten impurity ion bulk flow velocity at
the magnetic axis quantifies the net rotation of tungsten ions about the
torus axis at the innermost flux surface, where the gradient of poloidal
magnetic flux $\psi$ vanishes ($\nabla\psi = 0$). This on-axis value anchors
the full radial toroidal rotation profile and complements the edge
measurement given by [toroidal tungsten velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

The toroidal fluid velocity is the first velocity moment of the tungsten ion
distribution function $f_W$, summed over all ionization states and projected
onto the toroidal direction $\hat{\phi}$:

$$
v_\phi^W = \frac{\int v_\phi \, f_W(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v}{\int f_W(\mathbf{v}) \, d^3v}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the individual particle velocity in the $\hat{\phi}$
direction.

Core tungsten rotation is driven by neutral beam injection torque, intrinsic
rotation, and radial momentum transport; in H-mode plasmas, on-axis values
range roughly $10^4$–$3\times10^5$ m s$^{-1}$, depending on beam torque and
intrinsic rotation contributions. Measurement is performed via
charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy of tungsten line emission. The
analogous quantity for lighter impurity species is [toroidal nitrogen
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), and for the main
ion species [toroidal hydrogen velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the tungsten ion flow is directed in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Electrical potential difference associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna, defined between the antenna conductor or feed and its reference
conductor. It is the general antenna-voltage quantity; specialized names
specify amplitude or another representation of the waveform.
items.documentation:
Electrical potential difference associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna is the scalar electric potential of the specified antenna conductor
or feed relative to its associated reference conductor or node. It
represents the antenna voltage waveform before any child name specifies a
particular reduction or representation of that waveform.

The signed antenna voltage is defined by the potential difference between
the antenna node and its reference node:

$$
V_\mathrm{ant}(t) = \Phi_\mathrm{ant}(t) - \Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)
$$

where $V_\mathrm{ant}(t)$ is the antenna voltage, $\Phi_\mathrm{ant}(t)$ is
the electric potential of the specified antenna conductor or feed,
$\Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)$ is the electric potential of its associated reference
conductor or node, and $t$ is time.

The scope is voltages intrinsic to ion-cyclotron-heating antenna hardware,
including antenna conductors, straps, or feeds when they are the defined
electrical node. The unqualified parent does not by itself specify an
instantaneous value, phasor, peak amplitude, root-mean-square value, or any
aggregation over antenna elements; those distinctions belong to qualified
child names.

The [voltage amplitude of an ion-cyclotron-heating
antenna](name:voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is a
specialized reduction of this antenna voltage waveform to its peak
magnitude. This parent is distinct from antenna current, generator voltage
not defined at the antenna node, and launched or absorbed radio-frequency
power.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric potential of the specified
antenna conductor or feed is greater than the electric potential of its
associated reference conductor or node.

items.name: neutral_particle_flux
items.description:
Neutral particle flux is the signed net number of particles of one neutral
atomic or molecular species crossing an oriented surface per unit area and
time, summed over internal states.
items.documentation:
Neutral particle flux is the local net number flow of particles of one
neutral atomic or molecular species through an oriented surface, divided by
its actual area. It counts crossings in opposite directions with opposite
signs, without selecting a fixed geometric or magnetic-field direction.

The flux is the surface-normal velocity moment of the neutral distribution:

$$
\Gamma_0 = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})\,f_0(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_0$ is the neutral particle flux, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen unit normal to the surface, $f_0$
is the velocity distribution of the specified neutral species summed over
its internal states, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The
integral covers all particle velocities.

The quantity includes all internal states of the specified species and
excludes ions and other neutral species. It equals the sum of the
corresponding [neutral internal-state particle
fluxes](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) through the same oriented
surface. It is not a one-way incident flux, a surface-integrated particle
rate, or the energy-weighted transport represented by [neutral energy
flux](name:neutral_energy_flux).

The [radial](name:radial_neutral_particle_flux),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), and [parallel neutral
particle fluxes](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux) are projections of the
same neutral particle-number transport onto their respective specified
directions. The general quantity instead uses the normal of the surface
under consideration and is not the magnitude of the particle-flux vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral particle flow crosses the
surface in the direction of its chosen unit normal.

items.name: vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Vertical (Z) component of the vacuum magnetic vector potential produced
solely by toroidal-field coil currents in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical component $A_Z$ of the vacuum magnetic vector potential is the
projection of $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ onto the vertical direction
$\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It
represents the $Z$-directed contribution of the vector field generated
exclusively by toroidal-field coil currents in the absence of plasma and
eddy-current contributions, forming part of the complete [vacuum magnetic
vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) vector $(A_R,
A_\phi, A_Z)$.

The vacuum magnetic field is related to the vector potential by

$$
\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the vacuum magnetic field,
$\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the vacuum magnetic vector potential, and
$\nabla \times$ is the curl operator. The curl is gage-invariant, whereas
$A_Z$ depends on the selected gage and is not itself a magnetic-field
component. The complementary radial component is
[radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential);
unlike
[vertical_magnetic_vector_potential](name:vertical_magnetic_vector_potential),
this quantity excludes plasma and eddy-current contributions.

Sign convention: Positive when $A_Z$ points in the direction of increasing
vertical height $Z$.

items.name: krypton_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Charge-state-summed number density of krypton ions at the top of the H-mode
pedestal, with neutral krypton excluded.
items.documentation:
Krypton ion number density at the top of the H-mode pedestal counts ionized
krypton particles per unit plasma volume at that locus.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Kr,ion}} = \sum_{z=1}^{36} n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Kr,ion}}$ is the total krypton ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{z+}}$ is the number density of krypton ions in charge state
$z+$, $z$ is the positive integer charge state, and 36 is krypton's atomic
number.

The quantity is evaluated at the top of the H-mode pedestal, whose position
is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all ionized krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton.

This entry is the pedestal-top specialization of
[krypton_density](name:krypton_density); it is a local value rather than the
volume-averaged quantity
[volume_averaged_krypton_density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density).

items.name: ion_temperature_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Ion temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of
the ion population averaged over ion species and evaluated at the plasma
side of a divertor-target sheath, distinct from the target material
temperature.
items.documentation:
Ion temperature at the divertor target is the thermal energy per particle of
the ion population averaged over ion species and evaluated at the plasma
side of a divertor-target sheath. It is a plasma boundary quantity for ions
at the downstream end of the scrape-off layer, not a thermodynamic property
of the solid target material.

For the ion population, the species-averaged target temperature is defined
from the ion kinetic thermal-energy moments by:

$$
T_{i,t} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{3 n_{s,t}} \int \lvert \mathbf{v} - \mathbf{u}_{s,t} \rvert^2 f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_s
$$

where $T_{i,t}$ is the ion temperature at the divertor target, $i$
identifies the ion population, $t$ identifies the divertor-target
sheath-edge locus, $s$ indexes the included ion species, $m_s$ is the mass
of species $s$, $n_{s,t}$ is its number density at the target sheath edge,
$\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $\mathbf{u}_{s,t}$ is the mean flow velocity
of species $s$ there, $f_{s,t}(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity distribution,
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and angle brackets denote
averaging over the included ion species.

This quantity applies exclusively to the ion population immediately upstream
of a specified divertor target and represents an intensive, per-particle
thermal-energy scale averaged over ion species. It is not an extensive sum
of ion energies or densities, and it excludes electron, neutral-particle,
and solid-target temperatures.

It is the ion-specific component of [temperature at the divertor
target](name:temperature_at_divertor_target). Unlike [electron temperature
at the divertor target](name:electron_temperature_at_divertor_target), it
describes ion kinetic thermal energy at the same plasma-side target locus.

items.name: area_of_correction_coil
items.description:
Non-negative full geometric area of the conducting material in one
correction-coil cross-section, taken perpendicular to the local conductor
path and treated as constant along the coil length.
items.documentation:
Non-negative full geometric area of the conducting material in one
correction-coil cross-section is the cross-sectional measure of the
electrical conductor on a plane normal to the local conductor path. It is a
property of one correction-coil conductor element, not a sum over separate
turns or parallel conductor elements.

The area includes the conducting material in that cross-section and excludes
voids, insulation, coolant channels, nonconducting supports, and any
winding-pack or coil-footprint area outside the conductor material. For
hollow or compound conductors, only regions that are part of the electrical
conductor are included.

It is distinct from radius_of_correction_coil,
[inner_radius_of_correction_coil](name:inner_radius_of_correction_coil), and
[width_of_correction_coil](name:width_of_correction_coil), which specify
particular dimensions of a cross-section; different cross-sectional shapes
can have the same area.

items.name: second_local_tangential_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element
items.description:
Signed radius of curvature of an optical element's beam-entry front surface
along its second object-local tangent, for cylindrical or toroidal surface
models.
items.documentation:
The second local tangential front-surface radius of an optical element is
the signed [radius](name:radius) of curvature in the normal section
containing the second local tangent and the front-surface normal. It
describes the beam-entry surface along an object-local direction, not an
externally defined vertical direction.

In the right-handed object-local frame $(\hat{X}_1,\hat{X}_2,\hat{z})$,
$\hat{X}_1$ and $\hat{X}_2$ are the first and second tangents at the surface
vertex, and $\hat{z}$ is the chosen front-surface normal. With planar tilt
removed at the vertex, the defining relation is:

$$
\frac{1}{R}=\left.\frac{d^2 z}{d x_2^2}\right|_{x_2=0}
$$

where $R$ is the signed second-local-tangential front-surface radius, $x_2$
is displacement along $\hat{X}_2$ from the vertex, and $z(x_2)$ is the
front-surface sag along $\hat{z}$ in this normal section, measured relative
to the vertex tangent plane. A flat section is the limiting case $1/R=0$.

This quantity applies to cylindrical or toroidal front-surface models. It is
a radius of curvature, not reciprocal curvature or the geometric [aperture
radius](name:radius_of_optical_element), and it does not describe the back
surface.

The [first-local-tangential front-surface
radius](name:first_local_tangential_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element)
describes the orthogonal normal section and need not equal this radius. The
accepted [vertical front-surface
radius](name:vertical_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element) denotes the
same object-local second-direction quantity despite its different
directional label.

Sign convention: Positive when the center of curvature of the front-surface
normal section lies on the $+\hat{z}$ side of the local tangent plane.
